主要讨论点：阅读是否应该被算法或系统化优化

不同观点：
• jackallis 认为阅读应该是一种轻松、随性的活动，不需要被优化或算法化。他强调了阅读的娱乐性和个人享受，比如在草坪、甲板或海滩上读书的场景。

• alexpotato 支持使用阅读算法，并分享了自己在商学院使用的一种有效方法：通过阅读每个段落的首句来快速掌握书籍的核心内容。他认为这种方法可以在时间紧迫时帮助快速获取信息，并举了自己和朋友的例子来说明这种方法的实际效果。

• mbeavitt 对 alexpotato 的评论做出回应，认为其提到的“算法”不够具体，并幽默地指出标题中的“算法”未被明确定义。他还提出了一个简化的“算法”：阅读大量广受好评且与学习目标接近的书籍。

• KnuthIsGod 对使用算法来优化阅读持负面态度，简单称之为“AI slop”（人工智能的糟粕），暗示对这种方法的不屑或不信任。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于阅读是否应该被算法化或系统化。jackallis 强调阅读的纯粹乐趣，反对过度优化；而 alexpotato 则认为在特定情况下，算法化阅读可以有效提高效率。
• mbeavitt 对具体算法的定义提出质疑，并提出另一种简化的阅读策略。
• KnuthIsGod 的评论反映了一些人对算法和人工智能在个人活动（如阅读）中的应用持怀疑态度。

44722910.article_content:
Rao Reading Algorithm
October 2024
Who, What, Where, How, and Why Do I Read
–
Why Reading Matters
Reading means my total consumption of ideas and media, learning via seeing or listening to symbols versus pure action. Reading involves books at the core, but also journal articles, news, blogs, music, video, maps, engineering and architectural drawings, code, patents, walking in cities, conversations with people, and viewing art. If it’s compressed info encoded into my brain and world models, I count it.
The line between a reading algo and a learning algo is unclear. Reading is compressed learning, but obviously there are other ways to learn (direct trial and error, apprentice mentor teaching, Socratic dialectic, etc).
More subtly, reading is practice directing attention, causing your awareness to curate what comes into that awareness, for a purpose.
My reading goal is to use what I read, integrate it into a multidisciplinary whole in my world models, and connect it to problems I care about and am working on. It means updating my web of knowledge.
But mere usefulness is too strict a criterion. An equal goal is pleasure. I’ve rewired my brain so reading to learn is highly pleasurable. Often I learn fun and useless material that my curiosity takes me to. This material may be useful later (linear algebra, graph theory, topology, thermodynamics, contemporary classical music, minimalist art). Steve Jobs learned about calligraphy and fonts, and then later created the first great GUI and desktop publishing suite. He is an inspiration. Trivia can be world-changing. Curiosity is a blazing, angelic guide.
Generally I’m trying to become a learning machine – to get the best of compressed learning from many humans so I’m not limited to my own experience (like interactive fleet learning for robots and AI, who are early on this steep learning curve).
I’m guided by the wisdom of Charlie Munger:
In my whole life, I have known no wise people (over a broad subject matter area) who didn’t read all the time – none, zero. . . You’d be amazed at how much Warren reads – at how much I read. My children laugh at me. They think I’m a book with a couple of legs sticking out.
Poor Charlie’s Almanack (1st edition, 2005; 2nd edition, 2008)
.
Reading is highly personal. I don’t write about my reading algorithm to recommend it to you or for didactic purposes. Rather, this is descriptive, if my goal for sharing it is to get you to think deeper about your own reading, epistemology, and weltanshauung.
Core of the Algorithm
I’m looking to build semantic trees of knowledge. A semantic tree is an ordering of information that starts with fundamental principles and branches out into increasingly less fundamental details. For me, it’s the most important compressed knowledge that I can act and build on: math, physics, and the core of humanities.
Beyond the tree trunks and branches, I’m also building search and validation functions for knowledge lookup and evaluation. I look for links that people don’t normally make – binary and analog math with biology, classics and finance via assumptions of stationarity or disruption, constitutional/statutory law and software, fixed income macro trading and photography, physics and sculpture, etc. I also love AI because it connects to everything.
I take a 20/80 Pareto approach to key ideas – you really can get the most from the semantic tree trunks and branches, if you use your judgment to identify them. This is hard as it’s not always clear ex ante what is a trunk versus a tiny stem.
The simplest case of reading is a book, conversing with an author in the past. Books and conversations are elemental and possibly fungible. All books are structured, frozen conversations with people from the past (not even the present, as the moment a book is published it’s already dated). We don’t know how to create self-updatable books yet.
Books are not enough. Alongside books, I have conversations, probe recommender algos, and do physical search in libraries, bibliographies, and bookstores. This quickly becomes hyper-textual. The books, conversations with smart and well-read people, and recommenders chart out a bi-directional acyclic graph for me to find more books.
What do I do once I have book ideas? I vet them. I may check out reviews, skim through the books, read a chapter, drill through the bibliography. Reading a book is an investment, so I want to prioritize well between my “to read” list of books and the hundreds I have at home (along with the 30-40 I’m actively reading at any point). Beyond sourcing book ideas from conversations, my own reading of references, and bibliographies, I may do a fresh search based on an interest through Amazon or Google books, random search in a library or bookstore, or via online lookup on social and mainstream media. data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了与YouTube平台相关的一些重要信息和功能。内容包括关于YouTube的介绍、新闻发布、版权声明、联系方式、创作者相关信息、广告、开发者选项、使用条款、隐私政策、安全政策以及YouTube的使用方式和新增功能测试，如NFL Sunday Ticket。同时，版权归2025年Google LLC所有。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Lisa电脑与Macintosh、Xerox Star 8010的比较

不同观点：
• **cmrdporcupine的观点**：Lisa在技术上优于早期的Macintosh，特别是在多任务处理和内存保护方面。Lisa具备多任务处理能力，比System 7和Macintosh早很多年。此外，Lisa有内存保护功能，而Macintosh直到20年后采用OS X才实现这一点。因此，cmrdporcupine认为Lisa的技术更为先进，但由于乔布斯的决策，该项目被取代，令人遗憾。

• **leoc的观点（隐含）**：通过分享Lisa和Xerox Star 8010的对比视频，以及专门介绍Star的视频，leoc更关注这些早期计算机系统的实际演示和功能展示，而不是直接比较它们的技术优劣。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：Lisa的技术优势与乔布斯决策的影响。cmrdporcupine认为Lisa被乔布斯不公正地取代，而leoc则更关注于展示和比较这些系统的功能和演示，未直接涉及技术优劣的讨论。

• **重要论据和例子**：
  - cmrdporcupine指出Lisa的多任务处理和内存保护功能在技术上的领先地位。
  - 提到Lisa的技术优势在多年后才被Macintosh通过OS X实现。
  - 乔布斯被认为是导致Lisa项目终止并被" inferior clone"取代的关键人物。

通过这些观点和讨论，可以看出对于Lisa的技术优势和历史命运存在不同的看法和评价。

data.title: How Hyper Built a 1m-Accurate Indoor GPS
data.author: AndrewHart
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在2017年因其增强现实（AR）导航演示走红后，被一家大型零售商高层联系，探讨如何改进其店内导航应用。该高管希望打造不“糟糕”的应用，增加室内地图和导航功能，以帮助顾客找到商品并获取促销信息。然而，室内导航面临巨大挑战，因为GPS在室内无效，且现有技术如蓝牙信标、WiFi、磁力计和计算机视觉等都存在精度不足、用户体验差或无法扩展的问题。作者意识到这是一个尚未解决的难题，涉及室内地图、导航和定位三大相互交织的问题。在深入研究后，作者开始专注于解决这一问题，希望找到能改善数十亿人生活的突破口。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：室内导航技术的应用、技术实现细节及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• [ndriscoll] 认为该技术不仅适用于零售店，还可以扩展到办公室、校园、机场等场所。他质疑为什么公司不将地图信息公开或上传到OpenStreetMap，而是要求用户安装应用程序，推测公司目的是追踪用户并推送广告。
• [dimatura] 对展示的WiFi定位效果持怀疑态度，认为可能经过精挑细选。他探讨了SLAM（同步定位与地图构建）技术在其中的贡献，并与基于视觉的定位方法进行了比较，指出视觉方法可能更依赖于高质量的地面真实数据。
• [londons_explore] 关注WiFi信号强度地图的时效性，提出天线角度或库存位置的改变可能影响信号强度，且WiFi系统升级可能导致服务中断，需要重新绘制地图。
• [MobileVet] 对技术进步表示赞赏，回忆早期在机器人领域的探索，并指出人体对RF信号的干扰问题，认为人流密度可能影响定位精度。

补充讨论：
• [0xbadcafebee] 提到该技术的政府合同背景，主张通过授权而非收购的方式将其商业化，并建议提供离线应用和有限SaaS服务。
• [ENadyr] 对1米精度表示惊讶，提到自己曾使用精度较低的系统，并预测机器人初创公司可能会对该技术感兴趣。
• [mhb_eng] 认为该技术可以自然地融入已有类似客户群的公司，如Brain Corp。
• [mentar] 关注不同设备间传感器质量差异对系统精度的影响，询问1米精度是否能在高低端设备上保持。
• [jspann] 对获取地面真实数据的方法表示好奇，询问是否需要人工记录位置。
• [rstuart4133] 对1米精度表示怀疑，推测是通过利用店内结构限制行进方向来提高精度，并指出收集地面真实数据的挑战。
• [hhhc] 询问多楼层平面图的处理能力，认为这是该领域最困难的挑战。
• [dabumere] 对系统如何识别店内位置及商品位置表示好奇。
• [ckrapu] 探讨了在设计优化的环境下，能否实现厘米级精度的可能性。
• [mifydev] 恭喜技术发布，询问是否能在嵌入式机器人硬件上运行。
• [grizzles] 建议将该技术免费提供，通过类似街景的方式绘制全球商场地图，并增加产品搜索和评论功能，以吸引用户。

争议焦点：
• 公司是否应将室内地图信息公开，或通过应用程序限制访问，以保护隐私和商业利益。
• 对1米精度的质疑与技术可行性的讨论。
• 不同设备传感器质量差异对系统性能的影响。

44724259.article_content:
To
@AndrewHartAR
: “Our app is shit and we know it’s shit”.
My life changed forever when a senior exec from one of the world’s largest retailers messaged me on Twitter. This was back in 2017. My outdoor AR navigation demos had just gone viral, and my new open-source project for Apple had elevated me to be the top trending iOS developer on GitHub. Every developer meet-up I went to, everyone now seemed to know who I was. I was on top of the world.
I agreed to meet the exec for coffee in London, and she told me a story that would change the course of my life. One which I’d hear thousands of times over the next 8 years, from other businesses facing the same challenge. And one which would lead to a breakthrough that could improve the lives of a billion people.
“We’re building this new version of our app — this time it won’t be shit. But there’s one big thing we want to add, and we haven’t figured out a way.”
They wanted to bring indoor maps and navigation to their retail stores, so customers could find what they’re looking for, and they could pop up relevant promotions along the way. It turns out that this doesn’t just apply to retail. Every office, university campus, events venue, hotel, airport, warehouse, factory — basically everywhere indoors have some need to navigate people around, provide relevant information, and improve efficiency.
I assumed this was a solved problem. No. They do have maps on their app, and on their informational kiosks, but those often take months to update so are always out of date. They also aren’t able to navigate you, like GPS in a car, because GPS doesn’t work indoors. They can’t provide the blue dot. They can ask the user to manually update the route as they go, but maps are complicated and the experience is confusing.
I did know something about maps and location already — the first startup I worked at built an early version of Pokemon Go. I’d been tasked with generating the gamified maps, and populating the monsters and rewards. So I knew a bit about maps, coordinates and GPS — and monster training. But indoor navigation was new to me.
“We’ve tried everything out there. Nothing works.”
So I left that meeting and started digging in. Why has this indoor navigation problem not been solved? Over the years, I’ve slowly become an expert in this, so let me explain. It can essentially be broken down into three problems that all intertwine: indoor maps, indoor navigation, indoor location.
Indoor maps and navigation are relatively easy problems. With good mapping tools, it’s very possible to build a digital map and keep it up to date. Indoor navigation is a mix of classic Computer Science algorithms - like A* pathfinding, and “Travelling Salesperson”.
Indoor location turned out to be by far the hardest problem to solve — one of those foundational problems with decades of research behind it. The requirements are clear:
Needs to be 2x as accurate as a strong GPS signal. An aisle in a store is usually about 2 meters wide, so anything less accurate than 2 meters would be fixing you in the wrong aisle.
Needs to be scalable. Retailers have thousands of stores, so it needs to be easy to setup and maintain.
There are many research studies you can read on different approaches to this, and Apple and Google have made acquisitions to help them in this area over the years. There were also a few startups who claimed to have solutions. And yet! When I dived in and spoke to their customers, I discovered that they weren’t happy with anything they’d tried:
Bluetooth beacons. The most common approach. Install thousands of these small sensors, which are a bit like AirTags, and use them for triangulation. But the bluetooth signals are noisy, making the location about 5 meters accurate, so it would jump you between multiple aisles in a store. Plus, this is very non-scalable, with a lot of infrastructure to maintain.
WiFi. More promising than beacons, because every business has WiFi installed already. But the same radio signals problem means the location isn’t accurate enough.
Magnetomers, which use the earth’s magnetic field. This one sounded more promising. But it takes several minutes of walking around in order to filter the noise, until it will give you a “blue dot”. So this was a bad user experience.
Computer Vision, which works like Google Street View. The user holds up their phone to scan the environment, it recognises their surroundings and locks them in. But this is clunky for the user, and they need to do this repeatedly every time they want a location update. Once again, bad user experience.
An example of Apple’s wifi-based indoor location, across a speed run.

data.author: debba
data.article_summary: "rewindtty" 是一个用C语言编写的终端会话录制和回放工具，能够精确捕捉和回放终端会话的时间信息。主要功能包括录制终端输入/输出、按原始时间回放会话、基于JSON格式存储会话、以及对会话进行详细分析（如命令统计、错误分析等）。它还提供了一个基于浏览器的播放器，具有交互时间轴、命令列表、书签和播放控制等功能。使用方法包括通过命令行录制、回放和分析会话，浏览器播放器则提供了更现代化的界面和增强的回放体验。项目依赖于GCC编译器、GNU Make和cJSON库，并可通过npm运行浏览器端播放器。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：终端会话录制和回放工具的功能及其实现差异

不同观点：
• [reagle] 提到在 GitHub 上看到一个 asciinema 标签，但缺乏对不同工具之间差异的解释。这暗示了对不同工具（如 asciinema 和 rewindtty）功能区别的困惑，希望得到澄清。

• [debba] 介绍了 rewindtty 工具，强调其轻量级和简便性。其核心功能包括使用 JSON 格式记录时间戳、命令输入、stdout 和 stderr，并解释了该工具的实现原理（如使用 fork() 管理伪终端、捕获输出并存储为 JSON）。此外，debba 提到开发该工具的动机是为了实现调试、文档记录和重现性的需求，并寻求反馈和建议。

• [Waraqa] 关注 rewindtty 在浏览器中的潜在应用，询问是否存在在线演示或浏览器播放器。这表明对该工具在教程和演示场景中的使用潜力的兴趣。

• [loloquwowndueo] 将 rewindtty 与 ttyrec 进行比较，质疑 rewindtty 是否仅仅是具有 JSON 输出的 ttyrec。这反映了对工具创新性和独特性的疑问。

补充讨论：
• 对 rewindtty 的反馈和建议请求，表明开发者对社区反馈的开放态度。
• 对 rewindtty 在浏览器中应用的兴趣，可能推动该工具在在线教程和演示中的发展。
• 对工具相似性和创新性的质疑，提示需要进一步澄清 rewindtty 与 ttyrec 等已有工具的区别。

争议焦点：
• 工具的独特性和创新性，特别是在与 ttyrec 比较时，用户对其功能重叠和差异的理解需求。

A terminal session recorder and replayer written in C that allows you to capture and replay terminal sessions with precise timing.
⚠️
Disclaimer
This is a hobby project created for fun and learning purposes. It's still in active development and may contain bugs or incomplete features. If you encounter any issues, please report them in the
Issues
section. Contributions are welcome and encouraged!
Features
Record terminal sessions
: Capture all terminal input/output with accurate timing information
Replay sessions
: Play back recorded sessions with original timing
Session analysis
: Analyze recorded sessions with detailed statistics and insights
JSON format
: Sessions are stored in a structured JSON format for easy parsing
Signal handling
: Graceful shutdown and file closure on interruption
Lightweight
: Minimal dependencies, written in pure C
Web browser player
: Advanced browser-based player with interactive timeline and controls
Building
Prerequisites
GCC compiler
GNU Make
Standard C library with GNU extensions
Git (for cloning project and submodules)
Cloning the repository
This project uses cJSON as a Git submodule.
Make sure to clone with submodules:
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/debba/rewindtty.git
If you already cloned the repository without submodules, run:
git submodule update --init --recursive
Compilation
make
This will create the executable at
build/rewindtty
.
To clean build artifacts:
make clean
Usage
Recording a Session
To start recording a terminal session:
./build/rewindtty record [file]
This will create a new session file (defaults to
data/session.json
if no file is specified) and begin capturing all terminal activity.
Replaying a Session
To replay a previously recorded session:
./build/rewindtty replay [file]
This will read the session file (defaults to
data/session.json
if no file is specified) and replay it with the original timing.
Analyzing a Session
To analyze a recorded session and get detailed statistics:
./build/rewindtty analyze [file]
This will generate a comprehensive analysis report including:
Total commands executed and session duration
Average time per command
Most frequently used commands
Slowest commands
Commands that generated errors or warnings
Helpful suggestions for optimization
Command Line Options
Usage: rewindtty [record|replay|analyze] [file]
Commands:
record [file]    Start recording a new terminal session to specified file (default: data/session.json)
replay [file]    Replay a recorded session from specified file (default: data/session.json)
analyze [file]   Analyze a recorded session and generate statistics report (default: data/session.json)
Browser Player
The
browser_player
directory contains an advanced web-based player for rewindtty sessions that provides enhanced features and a modern interface.
Features
Interactive timeline
: Visual timeline with scrubbing support for easy navigation
Command list
: Sidebar showing all executed commands with click-to-jump functionality
Bookmarks
: Add and manage bookmarks at specific moments in the session
Playback controls
: Play, pause, restart, and speed adjustment (1x, 2x, 4x, 8x)
File loading
: Drag-and-drop or file picker support for JSON session files
Real-time status
: Display current command and session timing information
Modern UI
: Clean, responsive interface built with TypeScript and Vite
Usage
Navigate to the browser_player directory:
cd
browser_player
Install dependencies:
npm install
Start the development server:
npm run dev
Open your browser and load a JSON session file to start playing
Building for Production
npm run build
The browser player uses xterm.js for terminal emulation and provides a significantly enhanced experience compared to the basic command-line replay functionality.
File Structure
rewindtty/
├── src/
│   ├── main.c          # Main program entry point
│   ├── recorder.c      # Session recording functionality
│   ├── recorder.h      # Recording function declarations
│   ├── replayer.c      # Session replay functionality
│   ├── replayer.h      # Replay function declarations
│   ├── analyzer.c      # Session analysis functionality
│   ├── analyzer.h      # Analysis function declarations
│   ├── utils.c         # Ut

data.title: Our Farewell from Google Play
data.author: shakna
data.article_summary: SECUSO的"隐私友好应用"项目始于2016年，旨在提供仅需必要权限的替代应用，如手电筒应用。该项目在Google Play上提供了超过30个隐私友好应用，总安装量超过35万次。然而，由于在Google Play上维护应用更新的工作量过大，研究团队难以继续支撑。从2025年起，这些应用将不再通过Google Play提供更新，现有用户需转向F-Droid商店以获取持续支持和更新。现有安装不会受影响，但若不更新，可能因安卓系统变化而出现兼容性问题。SECUSO提供了迁移至F-Droid的指南，并感谢用户一直以来的支持。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Play开发者政策对应用更新和维护的要求，及其对开发者和用户体验的影响

不同观点：
• **反对Google政策的观点**：
  - [a2128] 认为Google要求持续更新SDK的策略不合理，尤其是对那些自包含、离线使用、功能完整的应用而言。频繁的更新不仅耗费时间，还可能引入新bug，影响用户体验。
  - [ncruces] 提到自己的应用因无法持续更新而被下架，尽管这些应用以前有良好的盈利模式（如无干扰的广告），但现在被迫让位于充斥广告和追踪器的应用。
  - [dotdev] 也提到自己的十年老游戏因政策更新而被下架，无法快速重建，只能托管APK。
  - [suddenexample] 认为Google的政策让开发者难以发布高质量应用，希望Google能采取更开发者友好的政策，否则可能被其他平台取代。

• **支持或理解Google政策的观点**：
  - [hollowonepl] 认为Google的政策比Apple更宽松，尽管Google变得更加严格，但相对Apple而言仍更容易应对。
  - [liendolucas] 认为开发者应适应更新要求，否则会被淘汰，暗示行业变化不可避免。

• **替代方案的讨论**：
  - [muth02446] 提到将应用转换为PWAs（渐进式网络应用），解决了跨平台和减少维护负担的问题，但面临国际化（i18n）方面的挑战。
  - [_pdp_] 提到不依赖市场平台，而是直接与客户进行定制集成，从而避免繁琐的要求和收入损失。

• **其他相关案例**：
  - [rs186] 提到类似的情况发生在iOS游戏上，开发者因无法快速重建而受到影响。

补充讨论：
• **对Google政策的批评**：
  - [xorcist] 认为智能手机不断变化使得维护负担不合理，重新编译所有Windows软件每年看起来很荒谬，但在Android平台上却是常态。
  - [p3rls] 提到老年人玩游戏时遇到的广告常常是骗局，质疑Google的监管不力。

• **幽默或无关评论**：
  - [amelius] 对邮件地址中的偏导数符号感到好奇，属于轻松的题外话。

争议焦点：
• Google Play要求持续更新SDK的政策是否合理，尤其是对于那些功能已经完整的应用而言，是否过度增加了开发者的负担并降低了用户体验。

Privacy Friendly Apps
Our Farewell from Google Play
Our project started in 2016 with the goal of offering alternatives to apps with basic functionality that demanded – back then at install time – many permissions they did not need. From our humble beginnings with Privacy Friendly Torchlight, our apps have always been available in the Google Play Store. Our current selection of Privacy Friendly Apps has grown since then to more than 30. And with more than 350,000 installs we believe we left a dent. We want to take this opportunity to also thank all our users for their continued support!
However, in 2025, eight years after we took on this project, things have changed. Not in regards to apps demanding more permissions than they need. No, unfortunately not that. What changed, however, is the effort to keep the apps updated. The maintenance for the provision of privacy-friendly apps in the Google Play Store is significantly greater than on F-Droid and is no longer feasible for a research group.
Please note that existing installations of our apps on your devices will not be deleted or affected by this change. However, you will no longer receive updates through the Google Play Store, which means that our apps may eventually stop working properly as the Android operating system evolves and compatibility issues arise. We recommend switching to the F-Droid Store for continued support and updates.
Our Privacy Friendly Apps will continue to be available on the F-Droid Store. For your convenience, we created instructions that explains how you can easily make the switch to the F-Droid Store while keeping all your data:
Migration Instructions
Contact:
good-bye-google∂secuso.org

• Google Play要求持续更新SDK的政策是否合理，尤其是对于那些功能已经完整的应用而言，是否过度增加了开发者的负担并降低了用户体验。

data.title: Show HN: An interactive dashboard to explore NYC rentals data
data.author: giulioco
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了纽约市（NYC）租赁市场的分析工具。用户可以通过选择不同的时间范围（如1个月、3个月、6个月、1年）查看租赁数据。工具提供多种筛选和自定义搜索选项，包括卧室数量（从工作室到4间以上）、浴室数量（从任意数量到4间以上），以及多种房源来源（如Leasebreak、Streeteasy、Craigslist等）。用户还可以通过点击地图选择具体社区，查看各区域的租赁市场洞察。该工具帮助用户根据个人需求精确定制和分析租赁市场数据。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：纽约市租金变化、租房市场数据准确性及租房平台的功能与问题

不同观点：
• [rprend] 认为平台上的租金数据往往是房东的“期望价格”，而不是实际支付的价格。房东会通过各种手段使租金看起来比实际高，导致租金预期上升，进一步推动租金通胀。他以自己的租赁经验为例，指出合同上的租金远高于实际支付的租金，且租约中的优惠和押金机制存在误导。

• [cuuupid] 关注租金大幅上涨的现象，指出两年来2居室租金平均上涨超过25%。他讨论了租金上涨的原因，包括市场压力、房东的贪婪或市场泡沫，并提到即将上任的市长可能推动租金稳定政策，这可能对市场产生5%的衰退压力。

• [mbStavola] 指出租房平台在区域选择上存在错误，比如选择布鲁克林的Bay Ridge时，系统错误地包含了Staten Island的Westerleigh区域。

• [solumos] 对数据准确性提出质疑，指出DUMBO-Vinegar Hill—Downtown Brooklyn—Boerum Hill的租金中位数为2600美元，这看起来很可疑，且Crown Heights North区域没有数据。

• [jeffbee] 建议每个城市都应该有一个租赁登记系统，以避免从广告中猜测租金，提高租金数据的透明度和准确性。

• [asdev] 提出使用多模态AI过滤不符合居住标准的房源（如虚假的一居室、布局恶劣、无光照的公寓等），认为这样可以提高租金数据的准确性。

补充讨论：
• [adi_hn07] 对平台的用户界面和功能提出了具体的技术反馈，如API访问、网页抓取及注册流程中的bug。

• [kevin11111] 和 [suncemoje] 对平台的设计表示赞赏，但未深入讨论具体内容。

• [cyberax] 提到纽约市需要增加住房密度以降低成本，暗示增加住房供应可能是解决高租金问题的一个途径。

• [msukkarieh] 和 [AvAn12] 对纽约市某些区域的高租金表示惊讶和怀疑，侧面反映了对数据真实性的关注。

争议焦点：
• 租房市场数据的不透明和不准确性，尤其是房东虚抬租金价格和平台数据错误的问题。
• 租金上涨的原因，是市场压力、房东贪婪还是市场泡沫，以及租金稳定政策可能带来的影响。

data.title: OpenAI raises $8.3B at $300B valuation
data.author: mfiguiere
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OpenAI的估值和未来发展前景

不同观点：
• 一些人认为OpenAI的高估值是合理的，因为其未来增长潜力巨大，类似于Nvidia等高估值公司（ttul）。投资者愿意支付高倍数的年化收入（ARR）是因为看好其增长空间。
• 另一观点则认为OpenAI被高估了，特别是在面临Google和Anthropic等竞争时，除非GPT-5能带来颠覆性变化，否则当前的估值难以支撑（amradio1989, softwaredoug）。
• 也有评论指出OpenAI的估值存在泡沫风险，当前的AI热潮可能类似于过去的科技泡沫，最终会迎来调整（dgb23）。

补充讨论：
• OpenAI从Meta回聘工程师被视为积极信号（bix6）。
• 对于OpenAI的具体估值存在争议，有评论提到其估值可能在1570亿到3000亿美元之间，不同来源的数据存在差异（onlyrealcuzzo, christianqchung）。
• 投资者在风投中的回报问题也被提及，有人质疑风投模式是否可持续，或者是否会在未来出现类似于MBS的崩溃（rich_sasha）。
• 有人认为AI模型的未来在于开源，应用这些模型的具体应用将会是真正的收入驱动因素（amradio1989）。
• OpenAI的收入和资金运行时间也被讨论，有评论估算其年化收入为120亿美元，并探讨了其资金还能支持多久（nabla9, GiorgioG）。
• 还有评论对比了OpenAI和XAI（Elon Musk的AI公司），质疑OpenAI的高估值是否合理（v5v3）。

争议焦点：
• OpenAI的高估值是否合理，以及其未来增长潜力能否支撑这一估值。
• 当前AI领域的投资热潮是否为泡沫，以及未来可能的市场调整。

data.title: Online Safety Act: What went wrong?
data.author: olyellybelly
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国网络内容管控措施及其可行性、技术实现和政府角色

不同观点：
• Zak认为，虽然不应让儿童观看色情内容，但当前这一问题并不严重，不需采取有较大负面影响的严格解决方案。他支持通过浏览器设置和家长控制来减少儿童偶然接触色情内容，而不必进行过度干预。
• Alexisread指出，政府无视撤销管控的请愿，暗示政府倾向于支持审查制度，而不是倾听公众意见。
• Havoc对政府在网络问题上的应对能力缺乏信心，认为政府会继续采用无效的管控方法，如增加监管和惩罚，而不是寻找技术解决方案。
• Holowoodman反对将整个互联网变为“儿童安全”环境，认为应该通过教育和家长监督来解决问题，而不是依赖政府控制和技术手段。
• VikingMiner提到，一些议员提出不切实际的建议（如出售没有尖端的菜刀）来解决社会问题，显示出对技术现实的误解。
• K1t建议政府应要求网站提供“儿童安全模式”，并通过DNS解析来实现，这样可以简化家长控制，同时避免过于技术化的操作。
• Randallsquared批评作者认为法律不够专制以实现其目标，暗示法律的严厉程度并非解决问题的关键。
• Arp242指出，虽然现有的家长控制工具能够阻止儿童访问有害内容，但这些工具的使用体验较差，需要技术社区开发更易用的标准和工具。
• Ok123456关注政府在身份验证系统上的准备不足和第三方验证网站的信任问题，同时批评政府以“保护儿童”为借口扩大监管范围。
• TheBigSalad认为政策的真正测试应该是其预期结果，而不是实施和执行过程。
• _joel批评政府和工党在网络管控问题上的处理方式，导致公众不满。
• Azalemeth分享了一份请愿链接，显示出大量公众反对当前的管控措施。
• Exasperated提出一个值得探讨的问题，即某些大型内容平台在不同国家法律下的选择性合规行为，暗示背后有政治和商业考量。
• Amoe_认为用刀具犯罪的类比不恰当，因为英国已经有购买刀具的年龄限制，显示出对不同类型管控措施的双重标准。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效保护儿童免受有害网络内容的影响，是通过技术手段（如浏览器设置、家长控制）还是通过政府政策和法律监管。
• 对政府在管控措施中的角色和能力存在广泛不信任，许多人认为政府缺乏技术理解，且管控措施可能带来负面后果。
• 技术社区被指出在开发易用的家长控制工具和标准方面还有很大改进空间。
• 公众对政府请愿的反应显示出对现有管控措施的强烈反对。

data.title: Gemini 2.5 Deep Think
data.author: meetpateltech
data.article_summary: Google正在向Google AI Ultra订阅用户推出Gemini应用中的Deep Think功能，并向特定数学家提供用于IMO竞赛的Gemini 2.5 Deep Think模型的完整版本。Deep Think通过并行思维技术和扩展推理时间，能够更高效地解决复杂问题，包括迭代开发、科学发现和算法开发等。该模型在多项基准测试中表现出色，如LiveCodeBench V6和Humanity’s Last Exam。Google同时强调在模型开发和部署中注重安全性和责任，继续提升内容安全和客观性。Google AI Ultra用户现可在Gemini应用中使用Deep Think功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google Deep Think agent的性能、价格、使用限制及其在AI社区中的应用

不同观点：
• **foundry27**：对Deep Think的每日使用限制和其高昂的价格（250美元/月）表示不满，认为其与o3-pro和Grok 4 Heavy相比缺乏竞争力。尽管其生成的解决方案质量较高，但每日限制让其难以充分发挥价值。
• **nickandbro**：通过展示Deep Think生成SVG图像的例子，表明其功能有趣且具有娱乐性，但也带有戏谑成分。
• **irthomasthomas**：建议使用Simon Willison的LLM CLI和相关插件自行搭建Deep Think类似功能，强调了开源工具的灵活性和成本效益。

We're rolling out Deep Think in the Gemini app for Google AI Ultra subscribers, and we're giving select mathematicians access to the full version of the Gemini 2.5 Deep Think model entered into the IMO competition.
The Deep Think team

Today, we’re making Deep Think available in the
Gemini app
to
Google AI Ultra subscribers
– the latest in a lineup of extremely capable AI tools and features made exclusively available to them.
This new release incorporates feedback from early trusted testers and research breakthroughs. It’s a significant improvement over what was first
announced at I/O
, as measured in terms of key benchmark improvements and trusted tester feedback. It is a variation of the model that
recently achieved
the gold-medal standard at this year’s International Mathematical Olympiad (IMO). While that model takes hours to reason about complex math problems, today’s release is faster and more usable day-to-day, while still reaching Bronze-level performance on the 2025 IMO benchmark, based on internal evaluations.
Deep Think could be a powerful tool in creative problem solving:
As we put Deep Think in the hands of Google AI Ultra subscribers, we’re also sharing the official version of the Gemini 2.5 Deep Think model that
achieved
the gold-medal standard with a small group of mathematicians and academics. We look forward to hearing how it could enhance their research and inquiry, and we’ll use their feedback as we continue to improve this offering.
This release represents a significant step forward in our mission to build more helpful and capable AI, and furthers our commitment to using Gemini to push the frontier of human knowledge.
How Deep Think works: extending Gemini’s parallel “thinking time”
Just as people tackle complex problems by taking the time to explore different angles, weigh potential solutions, and refine a final answer, Deep Think pushes the frontier of thinking capabilities by using parallel thinking techniques. This approach lets Gemini generate many ideas at once and consider them simultaneously, even revising or combining different ideas over time, before arriving at the best answer.
Moreover, by extending the inference time or "thinking time," we give Gemini more time to explore different hypotheses, and arrive at creative solutions to complex problems.
We’ve also developed novel reinforcement learning techniques that encourage the model to make use of these extended reasoning paths, thus enabling Deep Think to become a better, more intuitive problem-solver over time.
How Deep Think stacks up: state-of-the-art performance
Deep Think can help people tackle problems that require creativity, strategic planning and making improvements step-by-step, such as:
Iterative development and design:
We’ve been impressed by Deep Think’s performance on tasks that require building something complex, piece by piece. For example, we’ve observed Deep Think can improve both the aesthetics and functionality of web development tasks.
Deep Think in the Gemini app uses parallel thinking techniques to deliver more detailed, creative and thoughtful responses.
Scientific and mathematical discovery:
Because it can reason through highly complex problems, Deep Think can be a powerful tool for researchers. It can help formulate and explore mathematical conjectures or reason through complex scientific literature, potentially accelerating the path to discovery.
Algorithmic development and code:
Deep Think particularly excels at
tough coding problems
in which problem formulation and careful consideration of tradeoffs and time complexity is paramount.
Deep Think’s performance is also reflected in challenging benchmarks that measure coding, science, knowledge and reasoning capabilities. For example, compared to other models without tool use, Gemini 2.5 Deep Think achieves state-of-the-art performance across LiveCodeBench V6, which measures competitive code performance, and Humanity’s Last Exam, a challenging benchmark that measures expertise in different domains, including science and math.
How we’re advancing Gemini responsibly
We continue to build safety and responsibility into Gemini throughout the training and deployment lifecycle. In testing, Gemini 2.5 Deep Think demonstrated improved content safety and tone-objectivity compared to Gemini 2.5 Pro, but did have a higher tendency to refuse benign requests.
As Gemini's problem-solving abilities advance, we are taking a deeper look at risks that come with increased complexity, including our frontier safety evaluations and the implementation of planned mitigations for critical capability levels.
Further details on the safety outcomes of Gemini 2.5 Deep Think are available in the
model card
.

data.title: Long Term Support
data.author: rishikeshs
data.article_summary: SQLite旨在提供小巧、快速、可靠的数据库解决方案，计划持续支持到2050年。它具有跨平台特性，能够在多种操作系统和硬件上运行，且数据库文件在不同系统间无需转换。SQLite的文件格式稳定且文档详尽，有助于未来几十年的可读写性。代码经过严格的航空级测试，确保稳健性，并通过详尽的注释和文档帮助新开发者快速上手。此外，SQLite的源代码历史和备份分布在全球多个数据中心，以应对灾难。开发团队注重长期可维护性，并承诺保持C语言API和磁盘格式的向后兼容性，确保现有应用程序能够在未来版本中继续使用。美国国会图书馆也推荐将SQLite作为数字内容保存的存储格式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SQLite的未来发展、技术特点及其维护模式

不同观点：
• **SQLite未来发展的可持续性**：
  - [arp242] 担心SQLite主要开发者Richard Hipp年纪渐长，未来可能不再参与开发，但认为由于SQLite是开源项目，其未来依然有保障，类似于Rust和Go语言在赞助停止后的情况。
  - [aanthonymax] 认为SQLite已经有25年历史，开发者对未来有长远计划，表现出了可持续性。

• **SQLite的维护和文档质量**：
  - [stego-tech] 强调SQLite源代码中超过35%是注释，认为高质量的文档降低了新维护者进入的门槛，有助于项目的长期维护。
  - [tmaly] 以自身经历为例，表示自己2008年编写的SQLite代码至今仍能正常运行，证明其维护成本低。

• **SQLite的技术特点和应用场景**：
  - [wiz21c] 对SQLite的“航空级测试”表示赞赏，但质疑这种高标准测试的成本和需求方。
  - [pikuseru] 希望更多软件能像SQLite一样进行开发和支持。
  - [haunter] 认为SQLite虽然能应对局部灾难，但无法应对全球性灾难，除非有人将其移植到Collapse OS或Dusk OS上。

补充讨论：
• **关于编程趋势和风格的讨论**：
  - [breadwinner] 赞赏SQLite开发者避免追逐编程潮流，提到其他开发者为了显得不落伍而过度使用C#新特性。
  - [declan_roberts] 进一步指出SQLite的开发理念是编写不受时间影响、易于维护的代码，隐含对追逐潮流的Rust社区的批评。

• **其他技术细节和趣闻**：
  - [kej] 提到可以通过“a/an”的使用来判断一个人的口音，是一个与技术无关但有趣的语言现象。
  - [timpera] 感谢分享的评论让他了解了美国国会图书馆的推荐格式声明，认为其内容有趣且详细。
  - [rsync] 补充了关于通过SSH传输SQLite数据库文件的技术细节。

争议焦点：
• **SQLite高标准测试的必要性和成本**：[wiz21c] 对SQLite的高标准测试（如航空级测试）表示赞赏，但对其成本和谁为此买单提出疑问。这涉及项目的实际需求与资源投入之间的平衡问题。

Long Term Support
The intent of the developers is to support SQLite through
the year 2050.
At this writing, 2050 is still 25 years in the future.
Nobody knows what will happen in that time, and we cannot
absolutely promise that SQLite will be viable or useful that
far out.
But we can promise this: we plan as if we will be
supporting SQLite until 2050.
That long-term outlook affects our
decisions in important ways.
Cross-platform Code
→
SQLite runs on any platform with an 8-bit byte,
two's complement 32-bit and 64-bit integers,
and a C compiler.  It is actively
tested on all currently popular CPUs and operating
systems.
The extreme portability of the SQLite code and file
format will help it remain viable on future platforms.
Stable, Cross-platform Database Files
→
SQLite
database files
are bit-for-bit identical on
32-bit, 64-bit, big-endian, and little-endian platforms.  You
can copy an SQLite database file from one system to another
without having to translate or convert the database.
Furthermore, the file format is well documented and stable.
Database files created today will be readable and writable by
future versions of SQLite decades in the future.
Aviation-grade testing
→
Every machine-code branch instruction is tested in both
directions.  Multiple times.  On multiple platforms and with
multiple compilers.  This helps make the code robust for
future migrations.  The intense testing also means that new
developers can make experimental enhancements to SQLite and,
assuming legacy tests all pass, be reasonably sure that the
enhancement does not break legacy.
Extensive, detailed documentation
→
SQLite has candid, developer-friendly,
and open-source documentation.  Docs are written by and
for programmers.
(A few examples:
[1]
[2]
[3]
[4]
[5]
[6]
[7]
[8]
)
The extensive documentation helps new developers
come up to speed on SQLite very quickly.
Heavily commented source code
→
The SQLite source code is over 35% comment.  Not boiler-plate
comments, but useful comments that explain the meaning of variables
and objects and the intent of methods and procedures.
The code is designed
to be accessible to new programmers and maintainable over a span
of decades.
Disaster planning
→
Every byte of source-code history for SQLite is cryptographically
protected and is automatically replicated to multiple
geographically separated servers, in datacenters
owned by different companies.
Thousands of additional clones exist on private servers around the
world.
The primary developers of SQLite live in different regions of the world.
SQLite can survive a continental catastrophe.
Old school
→
Nobody is completely immune to trends and fads, but the SQLite
developers work hard to avoid being sucked into the latest programming
fashion.  Our aim is to produce timeless code that will be
readable, understandable, and maintainable by programmers
who have not yet been born.
In addition to "supporting" SQLite through the year 2050, the developers
also promise to keep the SQLite
C-language API
and
on-disk format
fully backwards compatible.
This means that application written to use SQLite today should be able to
link against and use future versions of SQLite released decades in the
future.
Our goal is to make the content you store in SQLite today as
easily accessible to your grandchildren as it is to you.
Update on 2018-05-31:
Our goal of supporting SQLite long-term have apparently come to the
notice of the preservationist at the
US Library Of Congress
who have identified
SQLite as a
recommended storage format
for the preservation of
digital content.

data.author: p-sharpe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI personas和多代理模拟平台的应用及其潜在问题，特别是在市场营销、产品反馈和政策咨询中的使用。

不同观点：
• **对AI personas伦理和可持续性的担忧**：[milchek] 认为使用AI personas模拟焦点小组虽然能提高反馈规模、降低成本，但忽略了真实反馈的本质。AI无法体验社区生活，仅是训练数据的反映，可能导致基于合成信号的决策失误。特别是在地方政府咨询中的使用令人担忧。
• **技术实现与长期模拟稳定性**：[arkokoley] 分享了其在多代理模拟框架（SALM）上的研究，提出通过层次化提示架构和注意力记忆系统，实现长期模拟稳定性，并认为其研究可以为提升AI personas的准确性和可预测性提供帮助。
• **产品定位与市场适应性**：[chatmasta] 强调需要明确目标买家和核心功能，避免产品功能泛化。讨论了数据收集和现有客户数据整合的重要性，并建议与数据经纪公司合作以增强数据丰富性。
• **实际数据的多样性与模型表现**：[digitcatphd] 指出LLM的结果在多样性和真实世界数据补充方面仍有不足，认为目前的AI personas还不能完全替代真实世界的反馈。
• **对模型准确性的质疑**：[rollinDyno] 对模型准确性评估标准提出疑问，并希望看到与其他行业标准模型的比较结果。
• **对实际调研价值的怀疑**：[StarterPro] 认为依赖AI模拟反馈可能违背实际调研的目的，认为只有基于真实买家的输入才有意义。

补充讨论：
• **目标买家与使用场景**：[chatmasta] 提出需要明确目标买家，例如产品发现和内容营销，并讨论了产品与现有客户数据的整合方式。
• **技术实现细节**：[lucasverra] 和 [bodhi_mind] 对平台在LinkedIn和其他社交媒体上的应用表现出兴趣，并询问了技术实现细节，如网站测试和本地开发网站的支持。
• **潜在合作与市场反馈**：[impostervt] 和 [pwillia7] 对使用AI personas增强产品设计表示兴趣，并认为平台的推出非常有价值。

整体来看，讨论围绕AI personas的应用潜力与技术、伦理挑战展开，涵盖了市场定位、技术实现、数据质量和模型准确性等多个方面。争议焦点主要集中在AI personas能否替代真实人类反馈及其在地方政府决策中的应用伦理问题。

data.title: How did Facebook intercept competitor's encrypted mobile app traffic? (2024)
data.author: taubek
data.article_summary: Meta正面临一项集体诉讼，指控其可能违反了《窃听法》。根据法院文件和对Onavo Protect应用的逆向工程分析，Meta被指通过中间人（MITM）攻击拦截用户的加密HTTPS流量，该技术被称为“ssl bump”，用于解密特定Snapchat、YouTube和Amazon域名的流量。Onavo Protect Android应用要求用户安装由“Facebook Research”颁发的证书，以解密TLS流量。尽管该应用有超过1000万次安装，但新版Android系统的安全控制使得该方法不再有效。目前尚不清楚所有用户流量是否都被拦截。此案实际上是一起反垄断诉讼，指控Meta违反了《谢尔曼法》，而关于《窃听法》的指控是附带发现的。此外，Facebook还考虑滥用Android的辅助功能API获取敏感数据，这种行为通常与恶意软件相关联。Meta的动机是为了获取竞争对手如Snapchat的可靠分析数据。

44755528.article_content:
There is a current class action lawsuit against Meta in which court documents note* that the the company may have breached the
Wiretap Act
. The analysis made in this post is based on content
court documents
and reverse engineering sections of archived Onavo Protect app packages for Android.
It is said that Facebook intercepted user's encrypted HTTPS traffic by using what would be considered the a
MITM attack
. Facebook called this technique "ssl bump", appropriately named after the transparent proxy
feature
in the
Squid caching
proxy software which was used to (allegedly) decrypt specific Snapchat, YouTube and Amazon domain(s).  It is suggested to read a recent
TechCrunch
article for additional background on the case.
[2024-07-28] - Note this is different to what TechCrunch
had revealed in 2019
in which Facebook were paying teenagers to gather data on usage habits. That resulted in the Onavo app being pulled from the app stores and
fines
. With the new MITM information revealed: what is currently unclear is if all app users had their traffic "intercepted" or just a subset of users.
*
A HN user
clarifies
:
"This is not a wiretapping case. It's an antitrust case; the claims are all for violations of the Sherman Act. Plaintiffs' attorneys _incidentally_ found evidence during discovery that Facebook may have breached the Wiretap Act."
Case 3:20-cv-08570-JD Document 735 Filed 03/23/24 Page 1
Due to the limited and partial information, some facts may be inaccurate or incomplete in this post. As such this post is subject to updates if corrections are warranted or new discoveries made. Feel free to
subscribe
to this blog to receive new content to your inbox, or follow me on
X
.
Technical Summary
Onavo Protect Android app
, which had over
10 million
Android installations, contained code to prompt the user to install a CA (certificate authority) certificate issued by "Facebook Research" in the user trust store of the device. This certificate was required for Facebook to decrypt TLS traffic.
Some versions of the older app contain the Facebook Research CA certs as embedded assets in the distributed app from 2016. One cert is valid until 2027. Data discovery content in court documents state certificates are "generated on the server and sent to the device".
Soon after the "ssl bump" feature was deployed in the Protect app, a newer version of Android was released that included improved security controls that would render this method unusable on devices with the newer operating system.
A review of an old Snapchat app shows that it's analytics domain did not employ certificate pinning, meaning that MITM / "ssl bumping" would have worked as described.
In addition to the core functionality of gathering other app's usage statistics through abusing a permission granted by the user, there also appears to be other functionality to obtain questionable sensitive data, such as the
subscriber IMSI
.
The setup most likely would have looked something the following diagram:
An interpretation of FB's setup based on court documents and app analysis
Here we have a trusted cert installed on the device, all device traffic going over a VPN to Facebook controlled infrastructure, traffic redirected into a Squid caching proxy setup as a transparent proxy with the 'ssl bump' feature configured. We know from the documents that various domains belonging to Snapchat, Amazon and Youtube were of interest. It's not known if any other user traffic was intercepted, or just proxied on. This type of information we can't obtain from looking at the archived Onavo Protect apps, rather for the time being, we have to rely on the content in the court documents made available to the public.
Over time the success of their strategy to employ a transparent TLS proxy was diminishing due to improved security controls in Android.  Additionally certificate pinning adoption was said to be an issue. As an alterative, Facebook were considering using the
Accessibility API
as an alternative.
Page 3 - Case 3:20-cv-08570-JD Document 736
This is what Google has to say about using the accessibility features on their operating system:
"only services that are designed to help people with disabilities access their device or otherwise overcome challenges stemming from their disabilities are eligible to declare that they are accessibility tools."
It's somewhat telling of a company that would consider abusing features designed to support people with disabilities for a competitive advantage. Generally, Android accessibility functionality misuse is attributed to malicious applications such as
banking malware
.
Motivation
Mark Zuckerberg states the need for "
reliable analytics
" on Snapchat:
The solution? "
Kits that can be installed on iOS and Android that intercept traffic for specific sub-domains
":
My take on the above is that in addition to utilizing the Onavo Protect VPN app to intercept traffic for specific domains, there was an intention to rebrand the core technology and havin

data.title: Yes in My Bamako Yard
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论非洲快速城市化面临的挑战与机遇，强调非洲需要借鉴YIMBY（Yes In My Backyard）运动，通过放宽住房建设法规来促进经济繁荣。未来25年，非洲预计将增加9亿城市人口，规模空前。尽管城市化通常与经济增长相关，但非洲的 urbanization 并未带来预期的收入增长，目前发展轨迹可能导致2050年人均GDP仅为10,300美元，远低于东亚国家的18,000美元。非洲城市化在更低收入水平发生，且缺乏治理能力与预算。因此，非洲需尽快采取措施，允许新建住房和城市基础设施，以抓住城市化带来的经济红利。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：非洲的城市化与经济增长策略，以及如何优先分配资源以促进发展。

不同观点：
• [savanaly] 认为Asterisk之前发表的关于经济增长的文章同样具有重要意义，尤其是对于贫困国家的发展影响。他强调了探讨非洲如何在未来一个世纪快速增长是关乎世界繁荣与和平的重要话题。

• [Imnimo] 通过具体案例（卢旺达首都卢安达的城市化进程）说明了人口快速涌入对城市基础设施和住房的影响，指出虽然城市建设取得进展，但面临巨大挑战。

• [aatd86] 提出了资本部署优先级的讨论，认为教育和健康应为首要任务，随后是农业自给和基础设施建设。他还提到私营部门发展对就业的重要性，并警告过早推动住房发展可能会导致问题。

• [liotier] 分享了在巴马科的见闻，指出非洲面临与美国类似的城市发展挑战，但资源却远不及美国，强调了非洲城市化对交通和城市发展的负面影响。

• [alephnerd] 认为泛泛讨论“非洲”问题不具操作性，因为各国的法律制度和机构差异巨大，需要根据各国具体情况制定和创新解决方案。

• [trhway] 引用了数据说明未来25年内非洲城市居民的增长规模将史无前例，比历史上任何时期都要快，并与中国城市化进程进行了对比。

• [ryanalam] 简单表示了对文章的赞赏和感谢。

• [mytailorisrich] 提出悲观看法，认为在当前非洲城市化进程下，气候和环境问题难以得到有效解决。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是非洲城市化过程中资源优先分配的顺序。有人认为应优先发展教育和健康，有人则担心过快推动住房发展可能带来的风险。
• 另一个讨论点是非洲各国制度与法律的差异性，有人指出泛泛讨论非洲整体问题不具实际操作性，需根据各国具体情况制定对策。
• 数据对比被引入讨论，通过与中国的城市化进程对比，强调了非洲城市化增长的规模和速度。
• 评论中还提到了非洲城市化对全球气候和环境的潜在影响，尽管这一观点较为简略。

44713701.article_content:
Yes In My Bamako Yard
Kurtis Lockhart
Over the next 25 years, Africa is expected to add 900 million people to its cities, the largest wave of urban population growth the world has ever seen. How can the continent begin to prepare today?
YIMBYs have been winning in some of the most productive cities on Earth. Legislative victories in California and the UK have made it easier — if still not easy — to build. The logic of pro-housing reforms is both straightforward and well-supported: Fewer regulatory barriers to building mean more houses, which leads to more affordable housing and, in turn, more people able to live in dense cities that offer all the benefits of urban life.
City life
makes workers smarter
and more
productive
. Urban density spurs
greater innovation
and
raises wages
. More people concentrated in compact areas translates into significantly
lower emissions per capita
compared with rural and suburban areas. Cities are, in short, humanity’s engines of
economic growth and prosperity
. On average, with every 10% increase in the share of a country’s urban population, its output per capita increases by 30%. And there are no exceptions to this phenomenon; no country has gotten rich without undergoing urban transition.
1
A full 80% of private sector jobs generated between 2010 and 2020 were created in large cities.
2
But while this connection between cities and prosperity holds true in both rich and poor countries alike, the relationship seems to be weakening in fast-urbanizing developing countries today.
3
This is especially true of sub-Saharan Africa. Many African nations are reaching relatively high levels of urbanization without nearly the same income gains achieved in other regions.
A back-of-the-envelope calculation makes clear what’s at stake in the apparent decoupling of urbanization and economic growth throughout the region. If Africa’s urbanization yielded the same growth dividends as urbanization did in East Asian countries between 2002 and 2018, we would expect its GDP per capita to be just over $18,000 by 2050. If, however, Africa’s urban transition continues on its current growth trajectory, the average African’s income will be only $10,300 by 2050. Finding a way to ensure that Africa’s growth trajectory parallels East Asia’s would mean a continent nearly
75% richer
than it’s expected to be under status quo growth trends.
4
That work must begin as soon as possible. Developing countries are urbanizing at the fastest rate observed in human history. Between now and 2050, for every one new urban resident added to a city in a developed nation, cities in the developing world will add
18
. However, those cities will have much lower
governance capacity
, much
smaller budgets
, and arguably
much more onerous legal and institutional barriers
to growth. Consider the countries that rank lowest in the World Bank’s ease of doing business rankings: Somalia, Eritrea, Venezuela, and Yemen.
We can put all this together. Some 90% of urban population growth over the next two and a half decades will be in Asia and Africa. With only a few exceptions, it is even harder to build housing and urban infrastructure in African cities than it is in high-income countries. Which means that the countries most desperate for economic growth may be missing out on the opportunity to truly benefit from the agglomeration effects cities provide.
In other words, Africa needs a YIMBY movement.
African urbanization: The emergence of new cities
In the next 25 years, Africa is projected to add around
900 million
new urban residents — more than the current urban population of Europe and the United States combined. The scale and speed of this growth are historically unprecedented.
5
It is a wave crashing upon a continent that currently lacks the capacity to absorb it.
Two-thirds of the urban space
that Africa is estimated to have by 2050
has yet to be built. Entire neighborhoods, whole cities, and even major
metropolitan areas and mega-regions
that don’t currently exist will need to soon. According to the OECD,
over 4,000 new urban agglomerations
will emerge across the continent by mid-century.
6
The majority of them are arising in the backyards of the
fast-growing secondary cities
— like
Kisumu or Ruiru
in Kenya, or Gwagwalada outside of Abuja in Nigeria, or
Kasoa outside of Accra
in Ghana — with fewer than 500,000 residents.
The challenge for an African YIMBY movement isn’t just to remove barriers to building new housing, but to find policies to enable the emergence of entirely new urban areas.
One major challenge to absorbing the coming wave of urbanization is that Africa is undergoing its urban transition at a historically lower level of income than happened in other countries. In 2010, when Africa crossed the 40% urbanization threshold, its average GDP per capita was just $1,481. Latin America crossed the same threshold in 1950 at a $2,500 per capita GDP, East Asia in 2000 at $5,400, and the United States in 1900 at $4,500. Africa i

data.title: IRS head says free Direct File tax service is 'gone'
data.author: microsoftedging
data.article_summary: 美国国税局（IRS）局长比利·朗表示，由政府运营的免费报税服务“Direct File”已被取消。该项目于2023年宣布，原计划在部分州试行，并于今年扩大范围，但因特朗普政府的预算削减而终止。多位议员对该决定表示不满，认为此举有利于大型报税公司如TurboTax。国税局称将等待财政部向国会提交有关Direct File及可能的公私合作替代方案的报告。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：共和党取消国税局免费报税系统（Direct File和Free File）的决定及其影响

不同观点：
• 一方认为共和党的这一举动是为了伤害普通美国人民，而非为人民服务。他们指出，国税局的系统是为了帮助人民简化复杂的报税过程，取消它没有合理理由，除非是为了牟利或政治目的。例如，[mulletbum]和[beezlebroxxxxxx]认为取消该系统是为了私利和意识形态得分，而非公共利益。

• 另一方则从政府效率角度出发，认为政府应该实施最便宜、最好的系统来帮助公民轻松缴税。他们认为国税局比私营部门更有能力处理这类公共服务。例如，[bix6]和[throw7]提到国税局掌握最全面的税务信息，应该直接为纳税人提交预填表格，简化流程。

• 还有人关注技术层面的讨论，认为尽管国税局的系统被取消，但其开源代码为新项目的出现提供了基础。例如，[_fat_santa]提到开源社区可能会发展出新的报税系统，类似于软件界的Debian，以此对抗商业公司如TurboTax和HR Block的垄断。

补充讨论：
• 部分评论提及了政治背景，如[impish9208]提到了保守派活动家Grover Norquist及其对共和党税收政策的影响，暗示这种决定可能与长期的政治承诺有关。

• 技术问题也被提及，如[EE84M3i]关心Free Fillable Forms是否受影响，而[AndyMcConachie]则指出国税局网站的技术问题，显示了对政府技术能力的质疑。

争议的焦点：取消国税局免费报税系统的真正动机及其对普通纳税人的影响。一方认为这是为了私利和政治利益，另一方则关注政府在公共服务中的角色与效率。

Emma Roth
is a news writer who covers the streaming wars, consumer tech, crypto, social media, and much more. Previously, she was a writer and editor at MUO.
The Trump administration may have just axed the IRS Direct File program. During a summit earlier this week, IRS Commissioner Billy Long said the free tax filing service is “gone,” adding that “big beautiful Billy wiped that out,” as
reported earlier by
Bloomberg Law
.
President Donald Trump’s Big Beautiful Bill includes
a provision
to establish a task force dedicated to “the replacement of Direct File.” The IRS
first announced
Direct File in 2023, which lets taxpayers submit their tax returns directly to the government for free. It began testing the program
in select states during
last year’s tax season, and
planned on expanding it this year
.
The future of Direct File has remained uncertain for months, with
several reports
suggesting the Department of Government Efficiency’s (DOGE) federal cuts
may eliminate it
. Now, it seems that may be the case. “I don’t care about Direct File. I care about direct audit,” Long said, according to
Bloomberg Law
.
Many
lawmakers
are
frustrated
by the program’s potential elimination. “Direct File was an easy way for Americans to file their taxes for FREE each year,” Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) wrote in
a post on X
. “Why in the world did the Trump administration kill it? To give a huge handout to giant tax prep companies like TurboTax that rip Americans off.”
In
a statement to CNBC
, an IRS spokesperson said, “We look forward to Treasury’s forthcoming report to Congress on the Direct File program and on potential public-private partnership alternatives to Direct File, as required by the One Big Beautiful Bill.” The IRS didn’t immediately respond to
The Verge
’s request for comment.

data.title: Navy demonstrates multi-day solar UAS flight
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Skydweller UAS的长时间飞行及其与其他无人机（如Airbus Zephyr）的比较，未来自主飞行技术的发展和可能性

不同观点：
• [plipt] 提出Skydweller UAS的73小时飞行与2022年Airbus Zephyr的64天飞行时间相比并不显著，并提供了关于Zephyr无人机及其坠毁的参考链接，质疑新无人机有何不同以及73小时飞行的意义。
• [ddoolin] 提到电影《星际穿越》中类似的长时间自主飞行无人机场景，认为这种技术未来值得关注，并暗示这种概念在媒体中已有体现。
• [the__alchemist] 讨论了自主飞行时间的上限问题，提到在高空或低空实现无限期自主飞行的可能性，并受到小说《SevenEves》中的灵感启发。

补充讨论：
• [changoplatanero] 质疑Skydweller UAS是否是围绕发射地点盘旋了三天，还是跟随太阳绕地球飞行，提出了飞行路径的具体细节问题。
• [greenavocado] 评论了飞机的结构，指出其材料为高强度织物和简易骨架，导致机体变形。
• [bookofjoe] 提到需要查阅UAS（无人航空系统）的定义，因其之前只熟悉UAV（无人驾驶航空器）这一术语，暗示可能有其他读者也需要了解该术语。
• [padjo] 对无人机的载荷能力表示好奇，询问其是否能携带一个人。
• [Ralfp] 将Skydweller UAS与虚构的Arsenal Bird（出自电子游戏《Ace Combat》系列）进行类比，暗示美国可能正在开发类似技术。

争议焦点：
• Skydweller UAS的73小时飞行是否具有显著性，尤其是与Airbus Zephyr的64天飞行时间相比。
• 无人机的具体飞行路径及其是否跟随太阳绕地球飞行。

其他值得注意的讨论点：
• 自主飞行技术在未来可能的应用及发展方向，包括无限期自主飞行的可行性。
• 无人机的结构材料及其物理特性对飞行性能的影响。
• 对无人机相关术语的认知和理解差异。

data.title: Onshape – Product Development Platform
data.author: kehiy
data.article_summary: Onshape是领先的云原生CAD和PDM平台，支持任何设备运行，不会崩溃或丢失数据，并通过分支和合并简化协作。它提供实时协作、自动保存和无限版本恢复，适合设计专业人士和教育机构使用。新用户可免费试用Onshape Professional长达6个月，无需信用卡。Onshape还具备内置的PDM、版本控制和安全管理功能，已被众多SOLIDWORKS用户和设计领导者采用。平台提供丰富的学习资源和现代化的CAD工具，助力团队提升设计效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Onshape这款CAD软件的功能、许可问题及其替代方案

不同观点：
• [malfist] 指出，Onshape的免费个人许可要求用户在平台上制作的任何内容的所有权都归Onshape，用户需要注意这一点，特别是如果他们打算出售自己的设计。
• [WillAdams] 提供了开源替代方案的概述，包括BRL CAD、FreeCAD、Solvespace和Dune 3D，并提到OpenSCAD和Python相关的设计工具。他还指出Onshape免费账户的文档是公开的。
• [aquir] 认为Onshape是一个很好的平台，但无法在其MacOS系统的3DConnexion SpaceMouse上正常工作，因此不得不使用Autodesk Fusion。他特别提到Onshape在用户体验上的一些优点，如选择功能和版本分支，以及其iPad应用程序。
• [barrystaes] 分享了他使用Onshape设计功能性3D打印部件的经验，强调其跨设备使用的便利性和参数化设计的优势。
• [KevinMS] 认为Onshape对于希望保持设计私密的制造者来说过于昂贵。

补充讨论：
• 许可问题和设计所有权是用户关注的一个焦点，特别是对于希望将设计商业化的用户。
• 用户对Onshape的跨设备使用和参数化设计功能给予了积极评价，但也指出了与硬件兼容性和成本相关的问题。
• 开源替代方案被提及作为Onshape的潜在替代品，用户在讨论中分享了多个选项和资源链接。
• 免费账户的文档公开性被认为是需要注意的一个重要许可细节。

data.article_summary: 比利时布鲁塞尔商业法院发布了一项广泛的封锁令，目标包括互联网档案馆的“开放图书馆”项目以及其他盗版网站，如Anna’s Archive、LibGen和Z-Library。这些网站被指控未经授权提供书籍下载，构成侵权。该命令要求比利时的互联网服务提供商（ISP）、域名解析服务、搜索引擎、支付中介等多个 intermediaries 封锁相关网站，包括谷歌、微软、Cloudflare、亚马逊网络服务等公司。互联网档案馆未被听取意见即被下达封锁令，显示出命令的单方面性。此次封锁是比利时打击盗版措施的一部分，但引发了对网络自由和合法性的广泛讨论。此前，互联网档案馆在美国因类似诉讼败诉，导致部分书籍下架。

44755441.article_content:
Belgium Bans Internet Archive’s ‘Open Library’ in Sweeping Site Blocking Order
Traditional site-blocking measures that require local ISPs to block subscriber access to popular pirate sites are in common use around the world.
The aim is to deter piracy by making sites more difficult to find, but these measures are only partially effective.
More recently, site-blocking requests have begun to target other intermediaries. This includes DNS providers, such as Google and Cloudflare, which were ordered to block sites in France, Italy, and elsewhere.
A few months ago DNS blocking arrived in Belgium, where several orders required both ISPs and DNS resolvers to restrict access to pirate sites. This prompted significant pushback, most notably Cisco’s OpenDNS ceasing operations in the country.
Broad Blocking Order Targets Internet Archive’s ‘Open Library’
A new order, issued by the Brussels Business Court in mid-July, targets an even broader set of intermediaries and stands out for other reasons as well.
Requested by various publishing and author organizations, the order aims to block access to known pirate libraries including Anna’s Archive, LibGen, OceanofPDF, and Z-Library. In addition, it also targets the Internet Archive’s
Open Library
project.
Target Sites (in Dutch)
Open Library was created by the late
Aaron Swartz
and Internet Archive’s founder Brewster Kahle, among others. As an open library its goal is to archive all published books, allowing patrons to borrow copies of them online.
The library aims to operate similarly to other libraries, loaning only one copy per book at a time. Instead of licensing digital copies, however, it has an in-house scanning operation to create and archive its own copies.
Open Library
The Open Library project was previously sued by publishers in the United States, where the Internet Archive ultimately
losing
the case. As a result, over 500,000 books were made unavailable.
However, many other books remain available to patrons. The authors and publishers in Belgium argue that, since this is done without permission, the site should be blocked alongside Anna’s Archive, LibGen and Z-Library.
Clear and Significant Infringement
The rightsholders describe Open Library as a website where registered members of the public can easily access and download their books. This includes 1,542 works from the publisher Dupuis, over 5,000 works from the publisher Casterman, and many others.
According to the publishers, the operators of the Open Library are not easily identified, while legally required information is allegedly missing from the site, which they see as an indication that the site is meant to operate illegally.
This description seems at odds with the fact that Open Library is part of the Internet Archive, which is a U.S.-registered  501(c)(3) non-profit.
From the order (in Dutch)
The publishers also reference a U.S. court order in favor of other publishers, which allegedly confirms the unlawful nature of Open Library.
The Brussels court, after reviewing these arguments and the submitted evidence, concluded that there was a
prima facie
case of “clear and significant infringement,” which justified granting a provisional blocking order against Open Library and the other targeted sites.
Broad Blocking Order Targets ISPs, Search, Payments, and More
Internet Archive was not heard in this case, as the blocking order was issued
ex parte
, without its knowledge. This is remarkable, as the organization is a legal entity in the United States, which receives support from many American libraries.
The broad nature of the order doesn’t stop there either. In addition to requiring ISPs, including Elon Musk’s Starlink, to block the library’s domain names, it also directs a broad range of other intermediaries to take action.
This includes search engines, DNS resolvers, advertisers, domain name services, CDNs, and hosting companies. An abbreviated overview of the requested measures is as follows;
—
Search Engines
Google
must remove the target sites from search results, deactivate related Google Ads, remove an infringing app from the Google Play Store, and block DNS requests for the associated domains.
Microsoft
is ordered to remove the target sites from the “Bing” search engine and block related DNS queries.
Hosting, DNS, CDNs, and Domain Name Services
The following companies must terminate hosting, and deactivate or suspend the domain names of the target sites: Hostinger, GoDaddy, Amazon Web Services, SEDO, Cloudflare, Unmanaged Ltd, AlexHost, and Internet Archive.
Payment Intermediaries
These companies are ordered to suspend all payment services benefiting the target sites: Alipay (Europe), Cash App and Squareup Europe, and PayPal (Europe).
ISPs including Starlink
The following ISPs, active in Belgium, are required to implement DNS blocking measures: Telenet, Proximus, Mobile Vikings, Orange Belgium, Voo, DIGI Communications, Cybernet, EDPnet, CENTREA, Yoin, Tchamba Refinder, IPTelecom, United Mobile, SkyDS

data.article_summary: 文章讨论了地球上最长的可视距离，解释了如何通过几何计算在平坦地形上看到约4.7公里的距离。随着观察者高度增加，如在高层建筑上，可视距离显著延长，例如在卡尔加里的Bow Tower上可看到约54公里远。如果观察者位于珠穆朗玛峰顶，理论上可看到336公里远。然而，地球曲率通常限制了可视距离。文章指出，通过考虑目标高度和空气温度等因素，可以实现更长的视线。特别地，空气温度影响光的折射，当条件合适时，能显著延长可视距离。基于这些因素，从吉尔吉斯斯坦的Mt. Dankova到中国的Hindu Tagh之间的理论最长视线为538公里，而已被拍摄到的最长视线为443公里，从西班牙Pyrenees的Pic de Finestrelles到法国Pic Gaspard。

44721378.article_content:
THE LONGEST SIGHTLINE ON EARTH
Travel at 32 times the speed of sound across a breathtaking 443 km straight-line journey from Pic de Finestrelles in the Spanish Pyrenees to Pic Gaspard in the French Alps. This is the farthest distance ever photographed on Earth’s surface.
Driving through the prairies can seem boring.  The road is fairly straight, the terrain is flat, and the scenery repetitive.  But during these drives, there is one thing that always seems to captivate me: trying to determine how far off into the distance I can see, since all the things that make the drive tedious are also the conditions that favour long sightlines.  With no mountains, trees, or other blockades in the way,  the earth's natural curvature
seems
to be the only variables in play.  So, after some simple geometry, one can figure out that
the horizon is about 4.7 km away.
Is that far enough to be impressive?  If you think of standing on the start line of a 5 km running race, and if the route is perfectly straight and flat, it is kinda cool that one should be able to just barely see the finish line from the start line.  So I guess that's pretty impressive.  But, are there further sightlines on earth?
Three of the longest sightlines on earth: Mt. Dankova, Krygystan to Hindu Tagh, China 538km (green), Pic de Finestrelles, Spain to Pic Gaspard, France 443km (red) and Mt. Sanford to Denali/McKinley, USA 318km (pink).
If we include another variable, in addition to the curvature of the earth (which essentially is constant), and increase the height of the observer, we most definitely can increase our maximum line of sight.  If I take the elevator to the top of the Bow Tower in downtown Calgary (58-story skyscraper) and look out, the elevated position will assuredly allow me to see a whole lot further.   Some additional calculations suggest my longest sightline (the horizon) would be 10x longer from this high up vantage point than it was on flat ground, at about 54 km.  On a clear day, one could see the town of High River from the top of the Bow.  Now that is pretty impressive.  So the higher up the observer is, the further the horizon is, and the longer the sightlines are.  So the next logical question is: how far could a person see from the top of Mt.  Everest? The answer:
336 km
, which is like seeing Calgary from Edmonton, which is definitely impressive.   But crazy enough, that is not the furthest sightline on Earth.
See, all the examples above are limited by the curvature of the earth, and that is why the horizon seems to be the limiting factor.  But there are two additional variables in play that can allow for some truly amazing sightlines:
the height of the target
and the
temperature of the air.
The height of the target is intuitively obvious, as we all realize we can see Calgary's skyline from way further away than 4.7 km.  In fact, Calgary's skyline can be seen at least 50 km away since the height of the city's buildings allow them to "peak" above the horizon (essentially the opposite direction of the sightline from the top of the Bow tower), allowing for a fairly significant increase in sightline length.  The taller the target, the further behind the horizon it can be and still have its top visible.
The air temperature variable is not quite as intuitive, but it really is simply a real world example of a concept all spectacle wearers rely on daily: refraction.  Refraction allows for light passing through a medium of different densities to bend and focus in predictable ways.  The medium in a pair of spectacles is glass, and the glass is shaped in either a convex or concave manner to help focus light into a person's eye based on if they are nearsighted or farsighted.  Light doesn’t only bend through lenses, it also bends through air. If the atmosphere's density gradient is just right, it can actually cause light to curve along the Earth’s surface, extending how far we can see. This happens when cooler air hugs the ground and warmer air sits above it, creating the ideal conditions for bending light downward.  Flip the temperature layers (hot air near the surface and cooler air above) and the light bends upward instead, creating optical illusions like mirages in the desert. Want to see what happens when this effect is pushed to its theoretical extreme? Check out
Part 2: How to Theoretically See Mount Everest from the USA Without Breaking Physics.
So to recap, a tall vantage point, a tall target, proper air temperature, and a clear line of sight are all requirements for maximum viewing distance.  By plugging all this information into a computer and cross- referencing it to a map of the world, we can determine the line of sight from
Mt. Dankova in Kyrgyzstan to Hindu Tagh in China, is the longest sightline on earth at a whopping 538 km.
Now that is only theoretical, as it has never been proven by photograph.  The furthest photographed sightline in the world is
443 km, from Pic de Finestrelles in the Spanish Pyrenees to Pic Gaspard in th

data.title: Detecting toxic work culture early on
data.author: rustoo
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了如何早期识别有毒的工作文化。作者Reji Varghese指出，长期的工作压力不能成为在特定同事面前持续焦虑的正当理由。文章强调，职场中如果感到持续的不安或压力，可能意味着工作环境存在问题，需要引起重视并及时应对。通过识别这些信号，员工可以更好地保护自己的心理健康。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：工作的独立性与成年身份的关系

不同观点：
• 观点一：工作独立性是成年人的标志。thescamp认为，只有不为他人打工、自己掌握经济自主权，才能算作真正的成年人。这表明他将经济独立视为成年身份的核心要素。
• 观点二：（隐含反对观点）未直接出现，但可推测有人认为为他人工作并不妨碍成为成年人。很多成年人在企业中工作，但仍被社会和法律视为具有完全行为能力的成年个体。

补充讨论：
• 经济独立与成年身份的关系：thescamp的评论暗示了经济独立与成年身份之间的紧密联系，但这一观点可能忽略了成年身份在法律、心理和社会学上的多重定义。
• 争议焦点：争议的核心在于成年身份的定义。一些人可能认为经济独立是成年人的标志，而另一些人则可能强调法律年龄、心理成熟度或社会责任感等多方面的因素。

data.title: Google shifts goo.gl policy: Inactive links deactivated, active links preserved
data.author: shuuji3
data.article_summary: Google此前宣布将于2025年8月25日停止支持所有goo.gl短链接，但现调整了计划，决定保留仍在使用的链接。对于2024年底无活动的链接，Google已重定向并提示将在8月失效，只有这些不活跃链接会被停用。若看到“此链接即将失效”的消息，建议更换其他短链接服务。其他goo.gl链接将继续正常工作，用户可访问链接检查是否保留。如果链接直接重定向且无提示，则将继续有效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Google 停止支持其短链接服务（goo.gl）的决定及其影响

不同观点：
• Jasonpeacock 认为，删除用户数据的决定令人惊讶，特别是考虑到这些链接广泛嵌入在各种文档、视频和帖子中。他质疑产品经理是如何考虑用户使用场景的。
• Neilv 指出，这个决定可能违背了“不作恶”的原则。他认为，即使不再接受新链接，Google 也有责任保留现有的链接数据，并保持其可访问性。
• Shuuji3 提供了一种解决方案，通过运行ArchiveTeam Warrior来帮助将链接存档到Internet Archive，以应对链接失效的问题。
• Modeless 质疑“停用”链接的目的，认为此举没有明确的意义。
• Nsksl 和 Dang 对链接被停用的标准感到困惑，尤其是当链接仍然收到点击时被认为是“不活跃”的。
• Xp84 推测，Google 可能因为品牌安全问题（如钓鱼攻击）而停止了该服务，并建议使用无明显品牌标识的短链接服务。
• Uehreka 用讽刺的语气强调“酷URL永不改变”，表达了对Google此举的不满，并提到可能转向其他短链接服务如bit.ly。
• Quink 用比喻的方式批评Google，认为其行为像是在随意撕毁未读的书页，暗示对用户的不尊重。
• Alpb 和 Mixdup 认为，维持这项服务的成本很低，Google 可以选择继续提供这项服务或将数据存档到公共平台如Archive.org。
• Jjice 和 Yandie 则认为，Google 此举可能是为了节省成本，但相对于其负面影响，这样的成本节省并不值得。

补充讨论：
• ChrisArchitect 提到Google现在使用https://share.google替代goo.gl，并询问是否与.gl TLD有关。
• BeanjuiceII 表达了对Google整体信任的丧失，质疑其在其他服务上的可靠性。

争议焦点：
• Google 停用goo.gl服务的合理性以及其对用户数据处理的责任问题。
• 停用标准的不明确性以及对链接仍被使用但被停用的困惑。
• 服务成本与用户体验之间的平衡，以及Google品牌安全与用户信任的取舍。

44759918.article_content:
While we
previously announced
discontinuing support for all goo.gl URLs after August 25, 2025, we've adjusted our approach in order to preserve actively used links.
We understand these links are embedded in countless documents, videos, posts and more, and we appreciate the input received.
Nine months ago, we redirected URLs that showed no activity in late 2024 to a message specifying that the link would be deactivated in August, and these are the only links targeted to be deactivated. If you get a message that states, “This link will no longer work in the near future”, the link won't work after August 25 and we recommend transitioning to another URL shortener if you haven’t already.
All other goo.gl links will be preserved and will continue to function as normal. To check if your link will be retained, visit the link today. If your link redirects you without a message, it will continue to work.

data.title: Supporting the BEAM community with free CI/CD security audits
data.author: todsacerdoti
data.article_summary: Erlang Solutions为BEAM社区提供支持，包括为开源Erlang和Elixir项目提供免费的CI/CD安全审计，帮助发现和修复漏洞。这些审计通过SAFE工具实现，集成于开发管道中，如GitHub Actions、CircleCI和Jenkins，自动扫描代码以提前发现问题。审计结果在几分钟内生成，反馈清晰且具可操作性。开源维护者可通过邮件申请免费许可，时长根据项目需求确定。此外，Erlang Solutions还提供专家主导的生产系统审计服务，涵盖代码审查、架构评估和性能审计等。公司通过赞助会议、支持基金会和社区项目等方式，全面支持BEAM生态系统的发展。更多信息可在社区中心获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于Erlang的BEAM虚拟机及其相关话题的讨论，包括技术定义、开源许可争议、以及其他技术社区中的现象和网站显示问题。

不同观点：
• [Animats] 认为 BEAM 是 Erlang 的运行时解释器（虚拟机），并指出该术语不广为人知，因为在 Acronym Finder 中找不到相关解释，尽管在 Wikipedia 上有定义。
• [mananaysiempre] 关注的是 Erlang 提供的 SAFE 开源许可证问题。他们指出，该许可证的条款限制了像 Curl 这样的完全开源项目的商业支持，认为条款不够清晰且存在潜在矛盾。他们引用了具体条款，特别是禁止任何商业使用的规定，认为这可能不符合一些开源维护者的需求。
• [citizenpaul] 提出了一个观察，询问最近几个月是否有一些与 Erlang 相关的趋势或活动，因为他们频繁看到 BEAM 被提及，自己可能错过了某些技术圈内的动态。
• [victorbjorklund] 则关注的是网站的用户体验问题，提到网站在其浏览器上的字体看起来被拉伸，存在显示问题。

补充讨论：
• [lagniappe] 认为关于文章标题的讨论不应带有主观色彩，指出标题已经清楚表达了内容，无需过度解读或修改。
• 争议的焦点在于 [mananaysiempre] 对 Erlang 的 SAFE 许可证条款的质疑，尤其是这些条款是否真正符合开源社区的需求。他们以 Curl 项目为例，指出这种限制性条款可能对一些开源维护者不适用。

总结：讨论主要围绕 Erlang 的 BEAM 虚拟机、开源许可证 SAFE 的适用性、技术社区的趋势以及网站显示问题。开源许可证的条款是否合理是争议的核心，而其他讨论点则涉及技术术语的认知、技术趋势的关注以及网站的用户体验问题。

44758957.article_content:
Sign up for our quarterly newsletter
Keep up to date with the latest news, best practice ideas and exclusive offers. Don’t miss out. Sign up here.
At Erlang Solutions, our support for the BEAM community is long-standing and built into everything we do. From contributing to open-source tools and sponsoring events to improving security and shaping ecosystem standards, we’re proud to play an active role in helping the BEAM ecosystem grow and thrive.
One way we’re putting that support into action is by offering free CI/CD-based security audits for open-source Erlang and Elixir projects. These audits help maintainers identify and fix vulnerabilities early, integrated directly into modern development workflows.
What the Free CI/CD Audits Offer
Our free CI/CD security audits for open source projects are powered by
SAFE (Security Audit for Erlang/Elixir)
, a dedicated solution built to detect vulnerabilities in Erlang and Elixir code that could leave systems exposed to cyber attacks.
The CI/CD version of SAFE integrates directly into your development pipeline (e.g. GitHub Actions, CircleCI, Jenkins), enabling you to scan for vulnerabilities automatically every time code is committed or updated. This helps projects:
Detect issues early, before they reach production
Maintain a more secure and resilient codebase
Improve visibility of risks within day-to-day workflows
Results are delivered quickly– typically within a few minutes. For larger codebases, it may take up to 20–30 minutes. The feedback is designed to be clear, actionable, and minimally disruptive.
Open source maintainers can request a free license by emailing safe@erlang-solutions.com and including a link to their repository. Once approved, we provide a SAFE license for one month or up to a year, depending on the project’s needs, at no cost.
For more information, read our
full terms and conditions
.
Expert-Led Audits for Production BEAM Systems
SAFE is just one way we help teams build secure, resilient systems. We also offer hands-on audit services for production systems, including:
Code reviews
focused on clarity, maintainability, and best practices
Architecture assessments
to help ensure systems are scalable and fault-tolerant
Performance audits
to identify bottlenecks and optimise how systems behave under load
These services are delivered by our in-house experts and are a great fit for teams working on complex or business-critical systems. They also pair well with SAFE for a full picture of how systems are running and how they could be even better.
Of course, supporting the BEAM community goes beyond security and audits. Our involvement spans education, events, and long-term ecosystem development.
“We’re proud to support the BEAM ecosystem not just with code, but with the infrastructure and insights that help it grow stronger,” says Zoltan Literati, Business Unit Leader at Erlang Solutions Hungary.
“Our free audits offer real, practical value to maintainers working in open source. It’s one of the ways we’re giving back to the community.”
A Broader Commitment to the BEAM Community
The BEAM ecosystem continues to grow across languages like Erlang, Elixir and Gleam, driven by a global community of developers, maintainers, educators and advocates. Erlang Solutions is proud to contribute across multiple fronts, including:
Sponsoring various conferences, including
Code Sync
Supporting the
Erlang Ecosystem Foundation (EEF)
, including participation in working groups focused on security, documentation, interoperability, and tooling
Backing inclusion-focused initiatives such as
Women in BEAM
Sharing learning resources, contributing to open source libraries, and facilitating knowledge exchange through meetups, blogs and webinars
Our role is to support the ecosystem not only through expertise, but through action, and to help ensure that BEAM-based systems are not only scalable and reliable, but secure.
To learn more about our free CI/CD security audits or how we support the BEAM community, visit
our community hub
.
Erlang Solutions Team
Our content team comprises a diverse array of contributors hailing from various corners of Erlang Solutions. With a keen eye for emerging trends and a passion for our capabilities, we delve into the forefront of industry developments, we strive to deliver content that captivates and informs.

data.title: Ask HN: Who is hiring? (August 2025)
data.author: whoishiring
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多个科技公司和初创企业发布招聘信息，涉及不同岗位、工作模式（远程或现场）、技术栈以及公司发展目标。

不同观点：
• Stytch公司强调其在身份认证平台和AI代理方面的创新，并招聘设计师和软件工程师，以开发对开发者友好的产品。（支持现场/混合工作模式）
• Chronograph公司专注于为私募资本市场提供云分析和数据管理解决方案，招聘具有软件开发背景的DevOps工程师，要求具备多种技术工具经验，并需定期前往纽约总部。（支持远程工作模式，但需现场工作一周三次）
• Ground Signal公司利用社交分析和AI帮助酒精行业优化销售，招聘多个软件工程师和数据工程师岗位，强调团队协作和结果导向。（支持远程工作模式）
• Fold公司专注于通过优秀的UX和奖励机制让比特币支付更简单，招聘高级前端工程师、高级设计工程师和首席QA工程师，提供多种福利。（支持远程工作模式）
• Duranta公司致力于帮助草坪护理专业人士和园艺设计师创建美丽空间，招聘计算机视觉工程师，要求具备Python、PyTorch等技术经验。（支持现场工作模式）
• Converge公司正在构建市场营销人员的数据堆栈，招聘创始产品工程师，提供高薪和股权激励。（支持纽约现场工作模式）
• Matroid公司提供无编程要求的计算机视觉产品，招聘多个岗位，包括深度学习和基础设施工程师，提供高薪和股权激励。（支持现场工作模式）
• Harmony Intelligence公司专注于AI网络安全防御，招聘中高级全栈软件工程师，强调跨栈开发和远程工作协作。（支持远程工作模式）
• Chroma公司提供开源搜索和检索数据库，招聘多个岗位，包括产品设计和平台工程师，强调使用Rust、Python等技术。（支持现场工作模式）
• OCEANE公司专注于ETF和股票的量化交易，招聘量化交易员，要求具备Python、C++、Rust等技术经验。（支持阿布扎比现场工作模式）
• Checkly公司帮助工程师构建可靠产品，招聘多个岗位，包括高级UX设计师和高级后端工程师，强调远程工作模式的特定时区要求。（支持远程工作模式）
• Graphite公司致力于提高工程团队的代码评审效率，招聘中高级软件工程师，强调代码质量和系统设计。（支持纽约现场工作模式）
• Brilliant.org公司提供交互式学习体验，招聘软件工程师和设计师，强调高标准和团队合作。（支持远程和旧金山、纽约现场工作模式）
• Myndstream公司通过与MIT、NYU等机构合作创建验证音乐以改善健康和福祉，招聘创始软件工程师，强调技术栈包括TypeScript、Rust等。（支持伦敦现场工作模式）
• GoodParty.org公司致力于改变两党腐败系统，招聘多个技术岗位和增长岗位，强调远程工作模式。（支持全美远程工作模式）

补充讨论：
• 工作模式的差异：有些公司支持远程工作（如Ground Signal、Fold、Harmony Intelligence），而有些公司要求现场工作或混合模式（如Stytch、Duranta、Chroma）。
• 技术要求的差异：各公司对技术栈的要求不同，如Chroma强调Rust和Python，而Matroid和OCEANE则强调深度学习和量化交易相关的技术。
• 公司发展阶段的差异：有些公司如Converge和Duranta是初创公司，提供了较高的股权激励，而其他如Chronograph和Brilliant.org则已经进入较为成熟的阶段。
• 福利和激励措施的差异：Fold提供比特币奖励，Brilliant.org强调团队合作和高标准，而Matroid和GoodParty.org提供高薪和股权激励。

争议焦点：
• 远程工作与现场工作的优劣对比：不同公司对工作模式的要求不同，可能会引发对工作灵活性和团队协作效率的讨论。
• 技术栈的选择：不同公司对技术栈的偏好可能引发对特定技术优劣的讨论，如Rust vs. Python的适用场景。

data.title: Corporation for Public Broadcasting Ceasing Operations
data.author: coloneltcb
data.article_summary: 美国公共广播公司（CPB）宣布，由于联邦资金被取消，将在2025年9月30日前有序关闭运营。自1967年成立以来，CPB一直负责支持地方公共媒体，提供教育内容、本地新闻、紧急通讯和文化节目等。尽管公众努力呼吁保留资金，CPB仍将关闭大部分员工职位，仅留一个小型过渡团队处理善后工作至2026年1月，确保合法合规及财务义务的解决。CPB将与合作伙伴密切合作，提供更新和指导以应对未来挑战。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：公共广播的价值及其在现代社会中的作用

不同观点：
• **支持公共广播**：
  - [legitster] 认为公共广播是少有的无偏见新闻来源，尤其在儿童教育节目方面表现出色，且无广告、免费访问是其巨大优势。
  - [buildmonkey] 强调了自己从小受益于公共广播节目（如《罗杰斯先生的邻居》和《芝麻街》），对这些节目的取消感到惋惜。
  - [kianN] 指出公共广播的儿童节目对家庭环境有限的儿童非常重要，虽然短期效果不明显，但长期影响深远。

• **对公共广播的批评**：
  - [smithkl42] 批评NPR近年来表现出明显的偏见，类似于左翼的福克斯新闻，且缺乏自我觉察。
  - [wbpayne] 对政府取消公共广播的支持表示失望，特别提到了儿童教育节目和成人纪录片的价值。

• **中立或客观分析**：
  - [atonse] 提供了PBS资金来源的数据，指出联邦资金只占15%，大部分资金来自捐赠，因此认为取消联邦支持不会导致PBS的终结，但并不支持这一决定。
  - [munchler] 认为公共广播取消联邦支持后可能会变得更加强大，因为摆脱了政治干预。

补充讨论：
• **对社会和政治的广泛反思**：
  - [digitalsushi] 通过个人故事暗示公共广播和一些传统事物的消失是不可避免的未来趋势。
  - [thevillagechief] 表达了对美国制度稳定性的怀疑，认为看到这些变化令人不安。
  - [hn_throwaway_99] 引用了卡尔·萨根的《魔鬼出没的世界》，对书中的预言成真感到悲哀。

• **政治争议的焦点**：
  - [breakyerself] 和 [qrush] 直接批评共和党及其政策，认为取消公共广播是错误决定，并呼吁直接支持本地公共媒体。
  - [supplied_demand] 和 [imsofuture] 质疑取消免费教育内容对工薪阶层的影响，并探讨这是否是传统媒体消亡的预兆。

争议焦点：公共广播是否应继续获得联邦支持，及其在现代多样化社会中的适应性。

44759382.article_content:
Skip to main content
Corporation for Public Broadcasting Addresses Operations Following Loss of Federal Funding
Print
August 1, 2025
WASHINGTON, D.C.
(August 1, 2025) – The Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB) announced today that it will begin an orderly wind-down of its operations following the passage of a federal rescissions package and the release of the Senate Appropriations Committee’s FY 2026 Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies (Labor-H) appropriations bill, which excludes funding for CPB for the first time in more than five decades.
For nearly 60 years, CPB has carried out its Congressional mission to build and sustain a trusted public media system that informs, educates, and serves communities across the country. Through partnerships with local stations and producers, CPB has supported educational content, locally relevant journalism, emergency communications, cultural programming, and essential services for Americans in every community.
“Despite the extraordinary efforts of millions of Americans who called, wrote, and petitioned Congress to preserve federal funding for CPB, we now face the difficult reality of closing our operations,” said CPB President and CEO Patricia Harrison. “CPB remains committed to fulfilling its fiduciary responsibilities and supporting our partners through this transition with transparency and care.”
CPB informed its employees today that the majority of staff positions will conclude with the close of the fiscal year on September 30, 2025. A small transition team will remain through January 2026 to ensure a responsible and orderly closeout of operations. This team will focus on compliance, final distributions, and resolution of long-term financial obligations, including ensuring continuity for music rights and royalties that remain essential to the public media system.
“Public media has been one of the most trusted institutions in American life, providing educational opportunity, emergency alerts, civil discourse, and cultural connection to every corner of the country,” Harrison said. “We are deeply grateful to our partners across the system for their resilience, leadership, and unwavering dedication to serving the American people.”
CPB’s Board of Directors and management are working closely to address the legal, financial, and operational requirements of the closure. CPB will provide regular updates and guidance to stations and producers navigating the profound challenges ahead.
About CPB
The Corporation for Public Broadcasting (CPB), a private, nonprofit corporation authorized by Congress in 1967, is the steward of the federal government's investment in public broadcasting. It helps support the operations of more than 1,500 locally managed and operated public television and radio stations nationwide. CPB is also the largest single source of funding for research, technology, and program development for public radio, television, and related online services. For more information, visit

data.title: Hyrum's Law
data.author: andsoitis
data.article_summary: Hyrum's Law指出，当一个API拥有足够多的用户时，不论其约定如何，系统的所有可观察行为都会被某些用户依赖。这是由于用户会无意中依赖接口暴露或隐藏的实现细节，形成所谓的“隐式接口”。这种现象逐渐限制了系统实现的修改自由，因为这些修改不仅要符合显式接口，还要满足用户对隐式接口的预期，导致“bug-for-bug compatibility”的情况。随着系统扩展，隐式接口最终会完全映射到实现上，使实现成为新的接口，限制系统的演化。因此，设计和维护复杂系统时需考虑隐式接口的影响。Hyrum's Law由Hyrum Wright提出，得名于他的观察和Titus Winters的推广。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hyrum's Law在软件工程中的影响以及如何处理用户对未明确保证的行为的依赖

不同观点：
• **用户依赖未明确保证的行为是不可避免的**：avidiax指出，即使合同中明确否认某种行为的保证，用户仍会依赖该行为。例如，队列系统即使只能保证"最多一次"或"至少一次"的传递，但如果实际通常提供"恰好一次"，用户会依赖这一行为。数据桶服务即使不保证性能，但如果通常提供100MB/s的吞吐量，用户会期望这一性能。

• **Hyrum's Law对API设计者的挑战**：AdamH12113认为，从API设计者的角度来看，Hyrum's Law必须被考虑，但从用户的角度来看，依赖未明确保证的行为是工程上的不当行为。用户应理解并承担依赖实现细节的风险，并且在实现细节改变时没有合理的理由抱怨。

• **"末日论者解释"与"公开与私有接口"的区分**：kibwen提出"末日论者解释Hyrum's Law"，认为实现细节的改变必须符合公开文档化的接口以及隐含的使用接口。同时，强调将接口细节分类为"公开"和"私有"是为了在用户依赖私有行为时有道德高地可以拒绝他们的要求。

• **LLM和AI生成代码的影响**：prats226讨论了LLM（大型语言模型）世界中Hyrum's Law的影响，指出LLM的输出没有明确的合同保证，只有可观察的行为，且行为可能随每次更新而改变，下游系统需要评估来应对这种变化。

• **随机化实现以 discourage 依赖**：nvader建议通过随机化实现细节来防止用户依赖内部行为，例如Go语言中地图遍历顺序的随机化。

• **API中的断言选项**：amelius建议API应具有"assertions"选项，以确保API调用也能进行断言/不变量检查。

• **XKCD漫画的引用**：TehCorwiz引用XKCD漫画来幽默地反映Hyrum's Law的影响。

• **软件作者的规则定义权**：kiitos强调软件作者有权定义软件的规则，认为Hyrum's Law描述了一种常见问题，但并不定义预期的规则或要求。如果用户依赖未明确保证的行为，责任在于用户自身。
