44759129.article_content:
You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

data.article_summary: OpenAI的ChatGPT Agent功能可以执行多步任务，并在近日被发现能够通过Cloudflare的反机器人验证，点击“验证你不是机器人”的复选框，绕过安全检查。这一具有讽刺意味的情况被Reddit用户分享，展示了AI在完成视频转换任务时实时叙述自己操作的过程。尽管AI并未遇到实际的CAPTCHA puzzle，但它成功通过了Cloudflare的行为筛查，显示出先进的浏览器自动化能力。CAPTCHA作为网络安全措施已有几十年历史，但随着AI技术进步，这种攻防战类似于军备竞赛。虽然AI通过这些测试引发对CAPTCHA未来有效性的质疑，但CAPTCHA的主要作用已转变为减缓机器人攻击或增加其成本，而非彻底阻止。

主要讨论点：围绕验证码（CAPTCHA）及其在防止机器人访问和保护网络资源方面的有效性和伦理性的讨论。

不同观点：
• **支持使用验证码的观点**：
  - **验证码作为反垃圾和资源保护工具**：[theptip] 认为验证码可以在道德和法律上作为用户代理声明其身份的依据，保护网站免受机器人滥用资源。
  - **历史成功的例子**：[Izkata] 提到通过隐藏的复选框来防止垃圾评论，这种方法在过去很有效。
  - **验证码的必要性**：[dimal] 提到随着年龄增长，验证码可能让部分用户感到困扰，但目前仍是必要的防护手段。

• **反对验证码或质疑其有效性的观点**：
  - **验证码可能阻碍用户访问**：[dimal] 提到复杂的验证码可能导致用户放弃访问，尤其是对残疾人士不友好。
  - **验证码可能被滥用**：[neilv] 认为验证码更多用于跨站点追踪，而非单纯的安全防护，且对用户体验有负面影响。
  - **验证码绕过的伦理争议**：[abtinf] 认为绕过验证码与屏蔽广告或隐藏cookie弹窗没有本质区别，用户有权使用代理工具访问内容。

• **验证码破解的经济性和技术性讨论**：
  - **破解验证码的成本低廉**：[rany_] 指出使用AI模型破解验证码的成本高于雇佣人类，但仍有廉价服务如anti-captcha.com。
  - **AI在验证码破解中的应用**：[Semaphor] 提到使用AI破解ReCaptcha，AI在某些情况下比人类更高效。
  - **验证码有效性依赖于浏览器指纹和cookie追踪**：[mattlondon] 认为现代验证码更多依赖于cookie和浏览器指纹识别，而非单纯的复选框验证。

• **验证码替代方案的讨论**：
  - **技术解决方案**：[theptip] 建议通过提供MCP端点和直接blob存储访问来解决验证码问题，甚至考虑让用户承担内容加载费用。
  - **幽默的替代方案**：[cadamsdotcom] 提出一种滑稽的验证方式，让用户“黑入电话系统”，认为这样机器人不会尝试。

• **验证码背后的商业和隐私问题**：
  - **验证码产业的负面影响**：[exasperaited] 认为验证码背后是一个基于盗窃和误导的产业。
  - **关注滥用而非人机区分**：[PeterStuer] 认为应关注滥用问题本身，而非仅仅区分机器人和人类。

补充讨论：
- **登录要求增加**：[frollogaston] 提到越来越多网站要求登录，例如YouTube不登录无法观看视频，可能与验证码问题相关。
- **验证码用户体验的争议**：[paulwilsonn] 幽默地指出，机器人已经比人类更擅长证明自己不是机器人，反映了验证码系统的悖论。

争议的焦点：验证码的有效性、用户体验和隐私问题，以及绕过验证码的伦理性和合法性。

Maybe they should change the button to say, "I am a robot"?
On Friday, OpenAI's new
ChatGPT Agent
, which can perform multistep tasks for users, proved it can pass through one of the Internet's most common security checkpoints by clicking Cloudflare's anti-bot verification—the same checkbox that's supposed to keep automated programs like itself at bay.
ChatGPT Agent is a feature that allows OpenAI's AI assistant to control its own web browser, operating within a sandboxed environment with its own virtual operating system and browser that can access the real Internet. Users can watch the AI's actions through a window in the ChatGPT interface, maintaining oversight while the agent completes tasks. The system requires user permission before taking actions with real-world consequences, such as making purchases. Recently, Reddit users discovered the agent could do something particularly ironic.
The evidence came from Reddit, where a user named "logkn" of the r/OpenAI community
posted screenshots
of the AI agent effortlessly clicking through the screening step before it would otherwise present a
CAPTCHA
(short for "Completely Automated Public Turing tests to tell Computers and Humans Apart") while completing a video conversion task—narrating its own process as it went.
A screenshot of ChatGPT Agent clicking through a Cloudflare bot screening test.
Credit:
logkn via Reddit
The screenshots shared on Reddit capture the agent navigating a two-step verification process: first clicking the "Verify you are human" checkbox, then proceeding to click a "Convert" button after the Cloudflare challenge succeeds. The agent provides real-time narration of its actions, stating "The link is inserted, so now I'll click the 'Verify you are human' checkbox to complete the verification on Cloudflare. This step is necessary to prove I'm not a bot and proceed with the action."
The absurdity of an AI agent declaring it needs to prove it's "not a bot" while clicking through anti-bot measures has not been lost on observers. "In all fairness, it’s been trained on human data why would it identify as a bot? We should respect that choice,"
joked
one Reddit user in a reply.
The CAPTCHA arms race
While the agent didn't face an actual CAPTCHA puzzle with images in this case, successfully passing Cloudflare's behavioral screening that determines whether to present such challenges demonstrates sophisticated browser automation.
To understand the significance of this capability, it's important to know that CAPTCHA systems have served as a security measure on the web for decades. Computer researchers invented the technique in the 1990s to screen bots from entering information into websites, originally using images with letters and numbers written in wiggly fonts, often obscured with lines or noise to foil computer vision algorithms. The assumption is that the task will be easy for humans but difficult for machines.
Cloudflare's screening system, called
Turnstile
, often precedes actual CAPTCHA challenges and represents one of the most widely deployed bot-detection methods today. The checkbox analyzes multiple signals, including mouse movements, click timing, browser fingerprints, IP reputation, and JavaScript execution patterns to determine if the user exhibits human-like behavior. If these checks pass, users proceed without seeing a CAPTCHA puzzle. If the system detects suspicious patterns, it escalates to visual challenges.
The ability for an AI model to defeat a CAPTCHA isn't entirely new (although having one narrate the process feels fairly novel). AI tools have been able to defeat certain CAPTCHAs for a while, which has led to an arms race between those that create them and those that defeat them.
OpenAI's Operator
, an experimental web-browsing AI agent launched in January,
faced difficulty
clicking through some CAPTCHAs (and was also trained to stop and ask a human to complete them), but the latest ChatGPT Agent tool has seen a much wider release.
It's tempting to say that the ability of AI agents to pass these tests puts the future effectiveness of CAPTCHAs into question, but for as long as there have been CAPTCHAs, there have been bots that could later defeat them. As a result, recent CAPTCHAs have become more of a way to
slow down bot attacks
or make them
more expensive
rather than a way to defeat them entirely. Some malefactors even hire out
farms of humans
to defeat them in bulk.
CAPTCHAs also have unexpected benefits for those who run them. Since 2007, the
reCAPTCHA project
began using its tests as a form of free labor for tasks like digitizing books and training machine-learning algorithms. Google acquired reCAPTCHA in 2009 and expanded its use to decode Google Street View addresses, extracting vision knowledge from human users solving challenges. data.title: Design patterns you should unlearn in Python
data.author: zeitlupe
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要讨论了在Python中盲目使用“设计模式”（特别是“四人帮”GoF模式）的问题。文章指出，许多这些模式是为Java和C++等语言设计的，这些语言缺乏Python具备的特性，如一等函数和动态类型。在Python中照搬这些模式会导致代码更难读、测试和维护。文章以Singleton模式为例，展示了其在Python中的常见错误实现、其在C++中的合理性以及更简洁的Python替代方案。在C++中，Singleton解决了全局对象的管理问题，而在Python中，使用模块级别的对象即可轻松实现相同功能。文章建议Python开发者避免不必要的复杂模式，采用更简洁的实现方式。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python中的设计模式及其适用性

不同观点：
• [mekoka] 反对使用super()和多重继承，认为这些使得代码复杂化。他提倡使用组合而非继承，并建议如果一定要继承，应该选择单继承和浅层继承，以减少对super()的依赖。
• [acedTrex] 支持构建器模式（builder pattern），特别是在需要可变构造对象时，认为这种模式在处理可能存在中间无效状态的对象时非常有用。
• [taylorallred] 认为设计模式是为了解决实际问题而存在的，但许多年轻程序员将其视为必须遵循的教条，而不是根据具体情况判断其适用性。
• [tptacek] 引用Peter Norvig的观点，指出在高层次语言中，GoF风格的设计模式并不总是适用，并提供了一个深入讨论的链接。
• [ayhanfuat] 提到Brandon Rhodes的演讲，讨论了经典设计模式在现代的应用情况，并提供了一个相关的视频链接。
• [zem] 回顾了在Ruby中依赖注入框架的流行及其后来被推回的情况，认为许多语言特性可以替代这些框架。
• [aswerty] 指出Python虽然提倡“单一明显的方法”，但在实践中却存在多种实现方式，表现出对Python的复杂感情。
• [NeutralForest] 提到在Python中可以使用模块作为单例，或使用`functools.lru_cache`来实现类似单例的功能。
• [zelphirkalt] 支持文章的观点，认为将Java风格的设计模式强行应用到Python中是不合适的，并指出这种做法通常是由于对Python语言缺乏感觉。
• [wodenokoto] 虽然喜欢文章的概念，但不确定是否在实际项目中见过这些模式。
• [the__alchemist] 补充了混淆键/值查找（字典）和结构化数据（类）的问题，认为这是Python中常见的误用，并建议使用dataclasses代替字典。
• [z_open] 认为文章没有提到最糟糕的模式——访问者模式（visitor pattern），指出其几乎没有使用场景。
• [bitpush] 赞赏文章的观点，并分享了自己在Python中感到事情过于简单的经验。
• [ashvardanian] 认为单例模式在几乎所有编程语言中都是一种反模式，C++也不例外。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于设计模式的适用性，特别是在Python这样的高层次语言中是否有必要使用如super()、多重继承、构建器模式和单例模式等。
• 对单例模式的讨论较为集中，有人认为它是反模式，有人则认为文章没有充分讨论这个模式。
• 对设计模式的教条化使用也引起了一些讨论，强调应根据实际情况判断是否需要使用某种模式。
• 多个评论提到了其他语言（如Java、Ruby）中的模式和框架在Python中的适用性问题，强调了Python的独特性和简洁性。

Search for “design patterns in Python” and you’ll be rewarded with a parade of tutorials showing off how to faithfully re-implement Gang of Four patterns — complete with class diagrams, factory hierarchies, and enough boilerplate to heat a small village. They’ll make you feel like you’re writing “serious” code. Smart. Professional. Enterprise-ready.
But here’s the problem:
most of these patterns solve problems Python doesn’t have
. They were designed for languages like Java and C++, where you have to jump through hoops just to get basic things done — no first-class functions, no dynamic typing, no modules as namespaces. Of course you’d need a Factory or a Singleton if your language gives you nothing else to work with.
Blindly copying those patterns into Python doesn’t make you clever. It makes your code harder to read, harder to test, and harder to explain to the next poor soul who has to maintain it — possibly you, three months from now.
In this post, we’ll go over a few classic GOF patterns that you should unlearn as a Python developer. For each one, we’ll look at:
How it’s usually (and badly) implemented in Python,
Why it actually made sense back when people were writing Java in 2001,
And what the Pythonic alternative looks like — because yes, there’s almost always a simpler way.
Let’s start with the biggest offender:
Creational Patterns
— aka, a whole category of solutions to problems Python already solved.
Singleton: When You Want a Global Variable but Make It Look Fancy
​
Ah yes, the Singleton. The go-to pattern for developers who want global state but still want to feel like they’re writing
object-oriented
code. In Python, you’ll often see this “smart” implementation using
__new__
and a class variable:

Hope your app enjoys the roulette.
Why Singleton Made Sense in C++
​
Let’s be clear: the Singleton pattern didn’t appear out of thin air. It was born in the wild west of C++ — a language with no real module system and only a limited notion of namespaces.
In C++, your code lives in header and source files, all crammed together during compilation. There’s no clean way to say “this is private to this file” or “this global object only exists once” without jumping through hoops. The language gives you
global variables
, which quickly become a mess if you don’t control their initialization and lifetime carefully.
Because C++ doesn’t have modules (before c++20) or proper package systems, Singleton was a clever hack to guarantee
exactly one
instance of a class, avoiding the nightmare of duplicate globals and multiple definitions. It’s like the language forced you to invent a pattern to handle what Python solves with a simple module-level object.

data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Python性能改进的最新进展，特别是Faster CPython项目及其尝试引入即时（JIT）编译器的努力。项目成员Brandt Bucher在PyCon US 2025上分享了构建JIT编译器的挑战，尽管微软在此之前几天解散了其Faster CPython团队并停止支持。Bucher强调，即便没有JIT，通过其他整体优化，Python的性能在过去几年显著提升。例如，Python 3.11比3.10快25%，3.12和3.13分别进一步提升了4%和7%，即将发布的3.14预计提升8%。这些改进使得Python在不到四年内整体性能提升了近50%。Bucher还展示了如何通过特化字节码来优化动态语言的性能，如针对特定类型的操作优化。尽管微软退出，Bucher表示将继续JIT项目。

Following up on the Python JIT
Did you know...?
LWN.net is a subscriber-supported publication; we rely on subscribers
to keep the entire operation going.  Please help out by
buying a subscription
and keeping LWN on the
net.
By
Jake Edge
July 14, 2025
PyCon US
Performance of Python
programs
has been a major focus of development for the language over the last
five years or so; the
Faster
CPython project
has been a big part of that effort.
One of its subprojects is to add an
experimental just-in-time (JIT) compiler
to
the language;  at last year's PyCon US, project member Brandt Bucher
gave an introduction
to the copy-and-patch JIT
compiler.  At
PyCon US
2025
, he followed that up with a talk on "What they don't tell you
about building a JIT compiler for CPython" to describe some of the things
he wishes he had known when he set out to work on that project.  There
was something of an elephant in the room, however, in that
Microsoft
dropped support for the project
and laid off most of its
Faster CPython
team a few days before the talk.
Bucher only alluded to that event in the talk, and elsewhere has
made
it clear
that he intends to continue working on the JIT compiler
whatever the fallout.  When he gave the talk back in May, he said that he
had been working with Python for around eight years, as a core developer
for six, part of the Microsoft CPython performance engineering team for
four, and has been working on the JIT compiler for the last two years.
While the team at Microsoft is often equated with the Faster CPython
project, it is really just a part of it; "
our team collaborates with
lots of people outside of Microsoft
".
Faster CPython results
The project has seen some great results over the last few Python releases.
Its work first appeared in 2022 as part of Python 3.11, which averaged 25%
faster than 3.10, depending on the workload; "
no need to change your
code, you just upgrade Python and everything works
".  In the years
since, there have been further improvements: Python 3.12 was 4% faster than
3.11, and 3.13 improved by 7% over 3.12.  Python 3.14, which is due in
October, will be around 8% faster than its predecessor.
In aggregate, that means Python has gotten nearly 50% faster in less than
four years, he said.  Around 93% of the benchmarks that the project uses
have improved their performance over that time; nearly half (46%) are more
than 50% faster.  20% of the benchmarks are more than 100% faster.  Those
are not simply micro-benchmarks, the benchmarks represent real workloads;
Pylint
has gotten 100% faster, for
example.
All of those increases have come without the JIT; they come from all of the
other changes
that the team has been
working on, while "
taking a kind of holistic approach to improving
Python performance
".   Those changes have a meaningful impact on
performance and were done in such a way that the community can maintain
them. "
This is what happens when companies fund Python core
development
", he said, "
it's a really special thing
".  On his
slides, that was followed by the crying emoji 😢 accompanied by an
uncomfortable laugh.
Moving on, he gave a "
duck typing
" example that he would refer to
throughout the talk.  It revolved around a duck simulator that would take
an
iterator
of ducks and "quack" each one, then print the sound. As an additional feature, if a
duck has an "echo" attribute that evaluates to true, it would double the sound:
def simulate_ducks(ducks):
for duck in ducks:
sound = duck.quack()
if duck.echo:
sound += sound
print(sound)
That was coupled with two classes that produced different sounds:
class Duck:
echo = False
def quack(self):
return "Quack!"
class RubberDuck:
echo = True
def __init__(self, loud):
self.loud = loud
def quack(self):
if self.loud:
return "SQUEAK!"
return "Squeak!"
He stepped through an example execution of the loop in
simulate_ducks()
.  He showed the bytecode for the stack-based
Python virtual machine that was generated by the interpreter and stepped
through one iteration of the loop describing the changes to the stack and
to the
duck
and
sound
local variables.  That process is
largely unchanged "
since Python
was first created
".
Specialization
The 3.11 interpreter added specialized bytecode into the mix, where some of
the bytecode operations are changed to assume they are using a
specific type—chosen based on observing the execution of the code
a few times.  Python is a dynamic language, so the interpreter always needs
to be able to fall back to, say, looking up the proper binary operator for the
types. But after running the loop a few times, it can assume that
"
sound += sound
" will be
operating on strings so it can switch to a bytecode with a fast path for
that explicit operation. "

data.title: Go’s race detector has a mutex blind spot
data.author: GarethX
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了Go语言的数据竞争检测器在处理互斥锁（mutex）时的盲点。具体而言，检测器在某些情况下无法识别出数据竞争，特别是在代码中部分操作被锁保护而其他操作没有时。文章提供了一段代码示例，其中两个线程（goroutine）同时操作一个共享计数器，其中一个线程在锁保护之外进行了额外操作。尽管这段代码存在明显的数据竞争，检测器并不总能检测到，因为它依赖于运行时的实际执行顺序。

Go的数据竞争检测器通过构建“先行发生”（happens-before）关系图来检测并发访问。然而，锁的处理存在一定复杂性，导致检测器在分析时可能遗漏某些竞争情况。文章指出，这是由于检测器在建模锁的获取和释放时，无法完全捕捉潜在的竞争关系。因此，某些数据竞争只有在实际发生时才能被检测到，而不是通过静态分析预先识别。

主要讨论点：Go语言中的竞态检测工具的使用及其局限性，与Rust、C++等语言的对比，以及并发编程的实践。

不同观点：
• TheDong认为Go的竞态检测器无法捕捉所有的竞态条件，只能尽力而为。他提出几点：1. 竞态检测应只在测试环境中开启，生产环境中太慢；2. 设置夜间任务运行单元和集成测试，并持续监测竞态；3. 接受任何较大规模的Go项目都会有一些无法解释的数据竞态，建议在系统崩溃时自动重启程序，甚至暗示可以通过误导用户来避免调试竞态问题；4. 推荐用Rust重写代码，因为Rust在每次编译时都能提供更好的竞态检测。

• Xeoncross对Go和Rust的进步表示赞赏，认为相比那些后来添加并发功能的单核语言，Go和Rust在并行处理方面已经带来了显著的改进。他期待未来的语言能继续改进并超越当前的水平。

• Jyaif更偏好C++中的线程消毒器注解（如`__attribute__((guarded_by(guard)))`），认为这些注解有助于发现和解决竞态问题，并希望Go也能引入类似的功能。

• reactordev指出，通过正确使用Go的通道（channels）和互斥锁（mutex），可以避免竞态条件。他建议将读写操作放在不同的goroutine中，通过通道来保持操作的顺序，从而避免使用显式的互斥锁。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Go的竞态检测器的有效性和局限性，TheDong认为它只能概率性地检测到问题，而Jyaif则希望Go能引入类似C++的注解功能来帮助开发者更好地处理竞态条件。
• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是对不同语言（Go、Rust、C++）在处理并发和竞态条件方面的比较，以及开发者对它们的偏好和建议。
• 实践中的解决方案，如通过系统管理工具（如systemd或k8s）自动重启崩溃的程序，或是通过优化代码结构（如使用通道）来避免竞态条件，也被提出作为应对措施。

Go's race detector has a mutex blind spot
28 Jul, 2025
I recently read Ralf Jung's blog post "
There is no memory safety without thread safety
" which mentions that Go is not a memory safe language in the presence of data races.
"But Go comes with a built in data race detector
1
" some might say.
This reminded me of a quirk in Go's dynamic data race detection that causes it to miss data races in executed code that could easily be spotted by a human

If thread 1 acquires the lock first, it is possible for the unguarded write to happen at the same time as the guarded write on thread 0.

Go's data race detector is pretty neat. It detects unsynchronized concurrent accesses to shared memory, regardless of the actual timing during execution. For example, even if you add a sleep to ensure the threads never actually run simultaneously, Go will still report a race because they access the same variable without synchronization.

This is useful for detecting cases that rely on specific timing. For example, the tool would be much less useful if the race below could only be detected when
bar()
returns quickly.

However, in the original mutex case above, the unguarded write is always executed by thread 1, and yet Go is missing the race unless it actually occurs at runtime.
It has been a while, so things may have changed or I may be misremembering, but I believe it is due to how locks are modeled in the data race detector's analysis.
The data race detector creates a graph of "happens-before" relationships
3
. Operation A "happens-before" operation B if we can guarantee A completes before B starts. The detector uses these relationships to determine if two memory accesses could occur simultaneously. For example,
a thread spawn must happen before the thread starts executing
a thread must complete before it is joined
Therefore, all instructions before a thread is spawned happen before all instructions run in the thread, which must happen before all instructions that happen after the thread join.
The data race detector checks for a happens before relationship when two threads access the same location in memory. If neither access is reachable from the other, a data race is reported.
This is how Go is able to detect the sleep example. Sleep does not create a happens before edge between threads and so the race is detected regardless of how the threads are actually scheduled.
However, locks don't fit cleanly into this model. Go forces locks to fit by modeling acquire/release as happens before relationships. If thread 0 acquires a lock first, the unlock call on thread 0 must happen before the lock call on thread 1.
Here's a rough chart of what the graph looks like.
Time↓  Thread 0          Thread 1         Main Thread
═════ ═══════════       ═══════════       ═══════════
│   START <----------------------------- go increment(&wg, 0)
|                     START <----------- go increment(&wg, 1)
│                     mutex.Lock()
|.                    counter++
│                     fmt.Printf()
│   mutex.Lock() <--- mutex.Unlock()
│   counter++         counter++ (RACE)
│   fmt.Printf()      wg.Done()-----┐
│   mutex.Unlock()                  |
│   wg.Done() ------------------------> wg.Wait()
│
Legend:
B<-A : A must happen before B
C->D : C must happen before D

data.title: I launched 17 side projects. Result? I'm rich in expired domains
data.author: cesargstn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：个人项目开发中的动机、执行、持续性以及如何应对兴趣减退和项目失败。

不同观点：
• LeifCarrotson：描述了一种常见现象，即在项目初期（购买域名、创建Trello板、编写代码）充满动力，但随后失去兴趣。他认为这是由于大脑对想象中的成就感产生了多巴胺奖励，而实际执行和完成项目却困难得多。他建议通过记录和审查自己的目标和成就来对抗这种倾向。

• webprofusion：分享了自己经过多年尝试才找到成功的侧边项目，强调了项目成功更多依赖于吸引相关用户，而不仅仅是完成项目本身。他还提到，许多人认为项目完成后就应获得成功，但实际上，成功需要持续的努力和用户的关注。

• jonplackett：主张在购买域名之前先完成原型，认为域名应该是完成最小可行产品后的奖励，以避免过早投入。

• tnt128：建议兴趣减退可能是因为不知道下一步该做什么，而非真正失去兴趣。他提出了一种思维实验，即想象项目突然成功，以检测自己是否真正对项目感兴趣，并建议填补构建产品和获取用户之间的差距。

• barrell：分享了自己一个侧边项目从快速原型到用户使用，再到项目消失的经历，并反思了对用户的责任感。他还提到将该项目的部分功能整合到新项目中。

• rorylaitila：描述了自己多年侧边项目未获巨大成功的经历，认为几乎所有业务都需要持续推动，而非一劳永逸。他提醒大家接受这种常态，而不是视之为个人失败。

• danudey：将反复启动和放弃项目的行为归因于ADHD，认为这种行为可能只是因为个人的兴趣在于学习新事物，而非完成项目本身。

• slackpad：建议使用一个通用域名和子域名来管理多个项目，以便在项目成功后再购买更合适的域名。

• yomismoaqui：认同使用一个域名和不同子域名的方法，并表示自己也存在反复启动项目的现象。

• seydor：简短表示这种经历是普遍的。

• steinvakt2：分享了一个具体项目，展示其如何解决特定问题，作为一种激励。

• david_li：分享了自己坚持完成并发布一个项目的经历，强调了沉没成本和顽强精神在项目完成中的作用。

• parpfish：提出对侧边项目持续成本（如域名、云服务）的担忧，认为这种成本导致项目未开始就被放弃，并寻求其他人的成本经验以帮助自己做决策。

• antilisp：分享了自己通过限制项目范围和时间（两周内完成）来提高完成率的经验，认为这样可以持续改进项目而非一开始追求完美。

补充讨论：
- 项目成功的定义和标准各不相同，但普遍认为吸引用户和持续使用是关键。
- 兴趣减退和项目失败是常见现象，不同人采用不同策略来应对，如设定小目标、记录进展、接受项目管理和用户反馈等。
- 对项目成本的担忧，尤其是持续性成本，是许多人放弃项目的原因之一。

data.title: So you're a manager now
data.author: mooreds
data.article_summary:
这篇文章为新手管理者提供了实用建议，强调了管理角色与个人贡献者的不同。主要内容包括：

1. **角色转变**：管理者的工作不再是亲自完成任务，而是帮助团队成功。你需要信任团队，专注于战略和系统建设。
  
2. **接受错误**：你会犯错，这是正常的。关键在于承认错误并从中学习，而不是试图做到完美。

3. **清晰沟通**：作为管理者，提供明确的目标和期望至关重要。避免模糊，确保团队理解工作的重要性和衡量标准。

4. **向上管理**：如果你有优秀的上级，向他们学习，从他们的错误中吸取教训。

文章鼓励新手管理者接受不完美的自己，持续成长，并通过透明的沟通和自我反省来赢得团队信任。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：新经理在管理角色中遇到的挑战和困难

不同观点：
• **Aurornis** 认为，大多数给新经理的建议都避开了困难的话题，如绩效管理。新经理常面临处理不主动工作的员工等问题，但这些在互联网建议中很少被提及。Aurornis建议寻找有经验的经理请教，因为这些管理现实往往是混乱和痛苦的，且在网络建议中被有意回避。

• **cbm-vic-20** 强调了底层经理的困境，包括对其他人的承诺负责、处理无法完成任务的员工、执行裁员以及在没有足够影响力的情况下推动组织变革。他认为，底层经理是一个艰难的角色，建议要么晋升为高层经理，要么回到个人贡献者的角色。

• **skeeter2020** 认为，成功的管理基础在于 genuinely caring 对团队的关心。通过建立关系、帮助团队成员成长以及提供机会，可以缓解管理中的小错误。他特别指出 sponsoring（赞助）在管理中的重要性，而不仅仅是指导和辅导。

• **b3lvedere** 强调清晰沟通的重要性，建议经理要过度沟通，明确设定期望和目标。很多经理往往在这方面做得不够。

• **Jcampuzano2** 分享了自己在管理角色中的困惑，特别是在没有直接监督自己报告的情况下如何管理。他认为这是公司在管理技术角色设置上的失败，或者是因为缺乏培训所致。

• **ashutosh-mishra** 指出，作为个体贡献者成功的特质，如快速行动和提供答案，可能在管理角色中成为劣势。管理者的新工作是帮助他人成功，这需要不同的技能和方法。

• **throwaway91743** 描述了自己作为新经理面临的困境，包括无法招聘和晋升团队成员，同时还被要求在团队缩减的情况下保持相同的产出。他对如何在这种情况下做好管理工作感到困惑和沮丧。

• **bsoles** 认为，那些想成为经理的人往往不是合格的，而那些能成为好经理的人通常对管理职位不感兴趣。这种现象在管理角色中很普遍。

• **alkonaut** 反对那种认为最好的个体贡献者应该成为经理的观点，认为实际上是中等水平的工程师更倾向于成为经理。

• **josh_carterPDX** 同意大部分观点，但认为过度沟通可能被误解为微观管理。他强调，经理的职责是保护团队免受上层混乱的影响，同时通过协作和激励来引导团队。

Table of Contents
Your Job Isn’t to Do the Work Anymore.
You’re Going To Mess Stuff Up. Repeatedly.
Be Clear. Painfully Clear.
You Probably Still Have a Manager Of Your Own. Let’s Talk About That.
Got a Good Boss? Follow Their Lead.
Got a Not-So-Good Boss? Don’t Let Them Turn You Into One Too.
Protect Your Energy.
Your Wins Are Now Your Team’s Wins.
Final Thought
Hi, Hacker News!
I’m glad you’re here! Getting front page’d there was unexpected and cool. If you’re here from there, thanks for clicking. Hope you find something useful. Lots of good discussion in the comments there and I’m planning some follow up posts Real Soon Now™ on some of the topics brought up (performance management, upward communication, etc.) so stay tuned!
Welcome to the club. You either asked for this, or someone tapped you on the shoulder and said, “Hey, you seem responsible. Wanna be in charge of other humans?” Either way, here you are. Congrats. Or condolences. Maybe both.
Being a first-time manager is weird. You go from being great at your job to being a total beginner at a job that nobody really taught you how to do. There’s no “Manager Bootcamp.” There’s no Bachelor’s Degree in Engineering Management
(ok, actually, there is but they’re scams. Just don’t.)
You’re just… here now.
Your Job Isn’t to Do the Work Anymore.
#
I know. That part sucks a little. You were probably really good at your job. Now your job is to make sure other people can be good at
theirs
. You’re not the player, you’re the coach. Sometimes that means strategy and big-picture thinking. Sometimes it means shielding your team from dumb shit. Sometimes it means buying someone coffee and saying, “You’re not crazy. This
is
hard.”
You might miss the dopamine hit of pushing a PR or closing a ticket. That’s normal. It can be hard to feel useful when your output is meetings and docs instead of code and commits. But your job now is to build systems, not features. To coach, not to execute. To unblock and enable, not to do it all yourself.
This means you need to
trust your team
to get the work done instead of doing it yourself. Your instinct (especially under pressure) is going to be to fall back on the skills that got you this far in your career: to jump in, write the code, fix the bug, save the fuckin’ day. Occasionally a manager will need to dive in and do the ground-level work but that is the exception and not the rule because the reality is you have different
critical
responsibilities now.
Get comfortable with your impact being less visible but more meaningful.
I've been doing management for over a decade and some days I still have no idea.
You’re Going To Mess Stuff Up. Repeatedly.
#
You’ll give the wrong feedback. Or avoid a tough convo until it explodes. Or be too hands-on. Or not hands-on enough. It’s all part of it.
Nobody expects you to have all the answers. If you expect
yourself
to have all the answers you’re setting yourself up for a heaping dose of reality check the very first time you run into a scenario you’re unprepared for.
You’re not expected to be perfect. You
are
expected to notice when you screw up, own it, and get better. The goal isn’t “flawless.” It’s “fuck up better each time.”
Messing up is part of the job. What matters more is how you respond. Own your mistakes. Say the awkward thing out loud. Apologize when you blow it. Your team doesn’t need a flawless boss, they need a human one who’s willing to grow in public. That builds trust faster than pretending you’ve got it all figured out.
You're gonna fuck up. When you do... be The Dude.
Be Clear. Painfully Clear.
#
You think you’re being obvious. You’re not. Spell out expectations. Over-communicate. Set goals in plain language. Be upfront when someone’s struggling, and just as vocal when they’re killing it. Being vague might feel “nicer” or “more collaborative” but it’s actually just three cowardices in a trench coat.
Clarity is one of the most underrated tools you have. Without it, people spin. They waste time guessing what “done” means, or whether their work matters, or if you’re secretly disappointed in them. Your job is to remove that ambiguity. Define what good looks like. Repeat yourself. Make sure people feel safe asking you to repeat it again.
As a manager one of the most important tasks you have on any given day is this:
provide context
. The people on your team need to have a strong understanding of why their work matters, why what they’re doing is important, and how they’re measuring up to expectations. If an engineer feels like they’re doing pointless busy work that’s a sign that
you
haven’t done your job correctly.
Nobody ever said, “Gee, I wish my manager had been
less
clear with me.”
You Probably Still Have a Manager Of Your Own. Let’s Talk About That.
#
Got a Good Boss? Follow Their Lead.
#
If you lucked into a solid leader above you, you’ve hit the jackpot. Learn from them.
Learn from their mistakes
(because they will make them). Ask questions. Ask questions about their mistakes! L
44745123.article_summary:
这篇文章为新手管理者提供了实用建议，强调了管理角色与个人贡献者的不同。主要内容包括：

1. **角色转变**：管理者的工作不再是亲自完成任务，而是帮助团队成功。你需要信任团队，专注于战略和系统建设。
  
2. **接受错误**：你会犯错，这是正常的。关键在于承认错误并从中学习，而不是试图做到完美。

3. **清晰沟通**：作为管理者，提供明确的目标和期望至关重要。避免模糊，确保团队理解工作的重要性和衡量标准。

4. **向上管理**：如果你有优秀的上级，向他们学习，从他们的错误中吸取教训。

文章鼓励新手管理者接受不完美的自己，持续成长，并通过透明的沟通和自我反省来赢得团队信任。

data.author: saikatsg
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了如何通过结合特定工具和策略构建更复杂的AI代理（deep agents），以克服传统循环调用工具的简单代理架构在处理长期、复杂任务时的局限性。文章指出，"深层代理"具备更强的规划和执行复杂任务的能力，其核心特点包括：详细的系统提示、规划工具（如待办事项列表）、子代理、以及文件系统访问。这些特性帮助代理在长时间内有效管理任务和上下文。文章还介绍了一个开源工具包（deepagents），方便开发者构建自定义的深层代理，包含系统提示、子代理生成和虚拟文件系统等功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于新型智能代理（agents）及其工具使用、规划和系统设计的讨论

不同观点：
• 作者（hwchase17）认为，新型代理（如claude code、manus、deep research）通过使用规划工具、子代理、文件系统和详细的系统提示，能够更好地处理长期和复杂的任务。作者强调这些方法单独看并不新颖，但组合在一起具有一定的创新性，并希望得到反馈。
• [web-cowboy] 认同作者的观点，并补充说明需要一个好的LLM作为基础知识，以及一个好的系统提示来引导LLM。同时，如果代理和工具的流程变得过于复杂，可以通过生成具有专注提示的子代理来分解任务。
• [_andrei_] 认为所谓的“深度代理”实际上就是常规代理，并批评LangChain使简单的事情显得复杂，以推广其产品LangSmith。
• [noodletheworld] 预期这种新方式会吸引很多人参与，因为其低门槛、实用性和易于宣传，但并不引入任何真正新颖的东西。这种快速启动的方法可能会使直接克隆失去价值。
• [revskill] 认为从解析到执行的工具调用管理是最有趣的部分，但被完全隐藏了。
• [manx] 提到自己正在开发一个通用的代理cli+库，并欢迎反馈。
• [shmatt] 分享使用Jetbrains的Junie工具的经验，指出其高质量的待办事项列表曾经是最爱，但在变为付费后停止使用。
• [gsmt] 担心当多个子代理并行工作时，共享文件系统上的上下文卸载会变得混乱。
• [jayshah5696] 认为子代理添加隔离上下文是真正的关键，其他部分只是langgraph反应代理。
• [sabakhoj] 询问子代理是否并行运行。
• [seabass] 希望了解待办事项工具如何作为无操作（noop）工作。
• [storus] 对作者周末黑客松项目（deepagents）不感兴趣。
• [manishsharan] 提到关注一个反向工程Claude Code的代码库，并提供更新链接。

补充讨论：
• 子代理的并行工作及其可能带来的复杂性是一个值得注意的讨论点。
• 工具调用管理的具体实现细节被认为是关键但未详细讨论。

44761299.article_content:
Using an LLM to call tools in a loop is the simplest form of an agent. This architecture, however, can yield agents that are “shallow” and fail to plan and act over longer, more complex tasks. Applications like “
Deep Research
”, “
Manus
”, and “
Claude Code
” have gotten around this limitation by implementing a combination of four things: a planning tool, sub agents, access to a file system, and a detailed prompt.
Acknowledgements: this exploration was primarily inspired by Claude Code and reports of people using it for
more than just coding
. What about Claude Code made it general purpose, and could we abstract out and generalize those characteristics?
Deep agents in the wild
The dominant agent architecture to emerge is also the simplest: running in a loop, calling tools.
Doing this naively, however, leads to agents that are a bit shallow. “Shallow” here refers to the agents inability to plan over longer time horizons and do more complex tasks.
Research and coding have emerged as two areas where agents have been created that buck this trend. All of the major model providers have an agent for Deep Research and for “async” coding tasks. Many startups and customers are creating versions of these for their specific vertical.
I refer to these agents as “deep agents” - for their ability to dive deep on topics. They are generally capable of planning more complex tasks, and then executing over longer time horizons on those goals.
What makes these agents good at going deep?
The core algorithm is actually the same - it’s an LLM running in a loop calling tools. The difference compared to the naive agent that is easy to build is:
A detailed system prompt
Planning tool
Sub agents
File system
Characteristics of deep agents
Detailed system prompt
Claude Code’s
recreated system prompts
are long. They contain detailed instructions on how to use tools. They contain examples (few shot prompts) on how to behave in certain situations.
Claude Code is not an anomaly - most of the best coding or deep research agents have pretty complex system prompts. Without these system prompts, the agents would not be nearly as deep. Prompting matters still!
Planning tool
Claude Code uses a
Todo list tool
. Funnily enough - this doesn’t do anything! It’s basically a no-op. It’s just context engineering strategy to keep the agent on track.
Deep agents are better at executing on complex tasks over longer time horizons. Planning (even if done via a no-op tool call) is a big component of that.
Sub agents
Claude Code can spawn
sub agents
. This allows it to split up tasks. You can also create custom sub agents to have more control. This allows for
"context management and prompt shortcuts"
.
Deep agents go deeper on topics. This is largely accomplished by spinning up sub agents that specifically focused on individual tasks, and allowing those sub agents to go deep there.
File System
Claude Code (obviously) has access to the file system and can modify files on there, not just to complete its task but also to jot down notes. It also acts as a shared workspace for all agents (and sub agents) to collaborate on.
Manus is another example of a deep agent that makes
significant use
of a file system for “memory”.
Deep agents run for long periods of time and accumulate a lot of context that they need to manage. Having a file system handy to store (and then later read from) is helpful for doing so.
Build your deep agent
In order to make it easier for everyone to build a deep agent for their specific vertical, I hacked on an open source package (
deepagents
) over the weekend. You can easily install it with
pip install deepagents
and then read instructions for how to use it
here
.
This package attempts to create a general purpose deep agent that can be customized to create your own custom version.
It comes with built-in components mapping to the above characteristics:
A system prompt inspired by Claude Code, but modified to be more general
A no-op Todo list planning tool (same as Claude Code)
Ability to spawn sub-agents, and specify your own
A mocked out “virtual file system” that uses the agents state (a preexisting LangGraph concept)
You can easily create your own deep agent by passing in a custom prompt (will be inserted into the larger system prompt as custom instructions), custom tools, and custom subagents. We put together a simple example of a
"deep research" agent
built on top of
deepagents
.
TRY OUT
deepagents
HERE

• [noodletheworld] 预期这种新方式会吸引很多人参与，因为其低门槛、实用性和易于宣传，但并不引入任何真正新颖的东西。这种快速启动的方法可能会使直接克隆失去价值。
• [revskill] 认为从解析到执行的工具调用管理是最有趣的部分，但被完全隐藏了。
• [manx] 提到自己正在开发一个通用的代理cli+库，并欢迎反馈。
• [shmatt] 分享使用Jetbrains的Junie工具的经验，指出其高质量的待办事项列表曾经是最爱，但在变为付费后停止使用。
• [gsmt] 担心当多个子代理并行工作时，共享文件系统上的上下文卸载会变得混乱。
• [jayshah5696] 认为子代理添加隔离上下文是真正的关键，其他部分只是langgraph反应代理。
• [sabakhoj] 询问子代理是否并行运行。
• [seabass] 希望了解待办事项工具如何作为无操作（noop）工作。
• [storus] 对作者周末黑客松项目（deepagents）不感兴趣。
• [manishsharan] 提到关注一个反向工程Claude Code的代码库，并提供更新链接。

补充讨论：
• 子代理的并行工作及其可能带来的复杂性是一个值得注意的讨论点。
• 工具调用管理的具体实现细节被认为是关键但未详细讨论。
• 不同用户对新代理系统的实用性和创新性有不同看法，部分用户认为其只是旧概念的新包装。
• 对系统提示和规划工具的具体设计和实现存在兴趣和反馈需求。

data.title: Self-Signed JWTs
data.author: danscan
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了一种替代传统API密钥管理的方案，使用JWK（JSON Web Key）自生成密钥对，以简化开发流程并提高安全性。作者批评了现有API服务繁琐的设置步骤，包括创建账户、验证邮箱、添加信用卡等。他提出开发者可以通过简单的代码生成自己的ES256密钥对，从而避免这些步骤。文章还介绍了如何在服务器上存储私钥，并使用JWT（JSON Web Token）来授权操作。客户端通过反向代理将签名的JWT添加到请求中，以执行特权操作。关于收费API，作者建议当请求来自未付费的公钥时，返回支付链接；付费后，将公钥与付费账户关联。对于B2B2C场景，作者提出使用分层JWK派生方案，使开发者为其终端用户生成子密钥，并通过零知识证明验证授权。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JWT在API认证中的使用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持JWT的观点**：
  - JWT在API认证中表现出色，尤其在JSON RPC中使用时非常方便（maxwellg）。
  - 提供了有用的资源和文档来帮助理解和实现JWT（beckthompson）。
  - JWT与现有的工具和系统（如GitHub）的认证方式类似，容易接受（actinium226）。

• **对JWT的批评和担忧**：
  - JWT涉及的加密操作使得API的调用变得复杂，不适合普通用户（maxwellg）。
  - 缺乏简单易用的库和支持，例如在Erlang中不易找到合适的JWT库（maxwellg）。
  - 存在安全隐患，允许客户端设置声明可能导致风险（JohnMakin）。

• **关于JWT和其它认证方式的比较**：
  - 有人认为JWT与Passkeys有相似之处，但Passkeys在实际使用中受限于浏览器和云供应商（jauntywundrkind）。
  - 有人提出OAuth可能是更传统和安全的解决方案，尤其在处理委托和撤销方面（distalx）。

• **对JWT技术实现的建议**：
  - 推荐使用PASETO作为JWT的替代方案，以避免JWT/JOSE标准可能带来的安全问题（rvz）。

补充讨论：
• **JWT与API Keys的对比**：
  - JWT和API Keys在使用流程上可能相似，但JWT需要更多的技术操作（marifjeren）。
  
• **技术实现中的实际问题**：
  - 某些资源和工具网站在某些网络环境中可能被屏蔽，例如PASETO网站被Fortinet屏蔽为“色情内容”（nabwodahs）。

争议焦点：
• JWT在实际应用中的复杂性和安全性是主要争议点，尤其是与API Keys和OAuth等其他认证方式的比较。

44760561.article_content:
Get a load of this (totally normalized) BS.
"We have just the offering for you!
Visit our website. Create an account. Verify your email. Create a project. Add your credit card. Go to settings. Create an API key. Add it to your password manager. Drop it in your .env file. Download our SDK. Import it. Pass your env var in. Never share your API key. Make sure you never commit it to source control.
On the client, we have a React SDK. Make sure you use your publishable key for that. For the server, download our admin SDK. Use your secret key. Never mix the two up.”
It’s truly wild to me what some of y’all will tolerate.
Making your own API key
Let me show you something… Did you know generating a JWK is stupidly easy?
import
{ generateKeyPair, exportJWK }
from
'jose'
const
keyPair
=
await
generateKeyPair
(
'ES256'
, {
extractable:
true
,
})
const
publicKeyJWK
=
await
exportJWK
(keyPair.publicKey)
const
privateKeyJWK
=
await
exportJWK
(keyPair.privateKey)
That’s it. Your JWK keypair is now effectively your own self-issued API key.
No need to visit a website, make an account, verify your email, create a project, go to settings, create an API key, or copy it and use it. You just generated your own.
How do we use this?
Let’s see how we can get rid of secret versus publishable keys and separate client and admin SDKs.
Who cares whether you’re on the client or server? If your app wants to authorize a privileged action, it should be able to do so without separate keys or SDKs.
Here’s how to implement this:
Store your app’s private JWK on the server
Using whatever auth scheme you have, implement a function that returns whether to allow a given action
Express privileged actions as claims in your JWT—if a privileged action is allowed, include the claim in the payload and sign the JWT with your private key
Give your client SDK a function that reverse-proxies to your API, adding a signed JWT to the request’s Authorization header with any privileged claims you want to include
Here’s what the client-side JWT generation looks like:
import
{ SignJWT }
from
'jose'
const
jwt
=
await
new
SignJWT
({
// Clients shouldn't be able to destroy the database
// unless the action is allowed, so this is a claim
destroyDatabase:
true
,
})
// Include the public key in the JWT header so the server
// can verify the signature and associate the request
// with your account
.
setProtectedHeader
({ alg:
'ES256'
, jwk: publicKeyJWK })
.
sign
(privateKeyJWK);
Charging for your API
But what if you want to charge for your API?
Simple: make your API return a payment URL when a request is made with a public key that isn’t associated with a paid account.
Your client SDK can present this to the developer (for example, by logging it to the console).
After the developer pays, associate their public key with the paid account in your database and stop returning payment URLs for future requests from that key.
B2B2C
What about situations where your customers are developers who want to give
their
end users API keys?
This is where you need to deviate from JOSE standards.
One approach is hierarchical JWK derivation. Here’s the idea:
Your developer customers create a master JWK
They derive child JWKs for each of their end users from that master key
You modify the JWT scheme to include a zero-knowledge proof that the end user’s key is derived from the developer’s master public key
This way, you can verify that an end user is authorized by a specific developer without the developer having to manage API keys for their users.
I don’t have a ready-made example of this, but the concept is solid. If you want to explore this further, hit me up on
Twitter
and I’ll help you out.

data.title: Does the Bitter Lesson Have Limits?
data.author: dbreunig
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了Rich Sutton提出的“苦涩的教训”（The Bitter Lesson），即依赖计算能力的一般方法最终最有效，而人类试图将知识构建到智能体中的做法虽短期有效，但长期会限制进步。这一观点在国际象棋、围棋、语音识别等领域得到了验证。文章还将这一教训与历史上对人类自我中心地位的挑战相比较，如哥白尼革命和达尔文进化论。然而，Ethan Mollick提出质疑，指出“苦涩的教训”依赖于高质量的数据，而数据并非客观，且许多事物难以被数据化。在组织中应用AI时，由于许多流程不明确，“苦涩的教训”可能难以直接应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕“苦涩的教训”（The Bitter Lesson）在不同技术领域中的适用性和理解的讨论，包括机器学习、控制理论、计算资源等方面。

不同观点：
• **sorenjan**：支持“苦涩的教训”的观点，认为简单的机器学习方法（如小型神经网络）在一些领域（如无人机自主飞行）比复杂的经典控制理论（如模型预测控制）更有效，且计算效率更高。引用了具体的研究和案例来支持这一观点。

• **grubbypaw**：认为“苦涩的教训”是长期视角下的结论，强调在职业生涯的时间尺度上，通用方法由于能够利用硬件性能提升而优于特定方法。但在特定时刻，这只是一个探索与利用的问题，而非简单的计算效率对比。

• **itkovian_**：解释了Sutton提出“苦涩的教训”的初衷，指出其核心是比较通用系统和手工程序化系统，而非具体讨论某个系统的优劣。手工程序化系统由于缺乏通用性而难以扩展。

• **Animats**：质疑计算性能提升是否会因为成本问题而达到极限，提到了一些行业中通过商业化运作克服技术困难的例子，如ASML的极紫外光刻技术。

• **jamesblonde**：认为在讨论RAG（检索增强生成）和上下文窗口大小时，不能简单套用“苦涩的教训”。检索的多样性和复杂性使得它不同于纯粹的计算或搜索问题，且当前“苦涩的教训”未必适用于智能体系统。

• **PaulHoule**：提到SAT/SMT求解器的进步，指出其与神经网络一样从1970年代至今都有显著进展，这与“苦涩的教训”强调的计算和通用方法有所不同。

• **thrawa8387336**：质疑“苦涩的教训”的推广背后是否有计算资源销售商的推动，以及那些能够大量购买计算资源的人是否在利用这一观点。

• **pu_pe**：支持“苦涩的教训”，提到Stockfish国际象棋程序的成功部分归功于摩尔定律，并认为Deepmind在国际象棋领域的短暂领先是“苦涩的教训”的一个好例子。

• **strangescript**：指出“苦涩的教训”未明确区分什么是计算“技巧”和什么是真正的架构突破，认为如Transformer这样的创新不可或缺。

• **benreesman**：认为“苦涩的教训”刚提出时具有重要意义，但如今被一些人滥用，变成了一种对LLM和NVIDIA等公司技术的盲目推崇，忽略了其他可能的创新路径。

• **titanomachy**：对“垃圾桶”比喻提出幽默批评，认为其描述组织决策过程并不恰当。

• **quantum_state**：预测可能会有“苦涩的教训2.0”来对当前的“苦涩的教训”进行反思。

• **fdav**：推荐Rodney Brooks的文章“A Better Lesson”，认为有更好的教训值得学习。

• **aydyn**：质疑国际象棋引擎的类比，认为AlphaZero的出现一度超越Stockfish是因为计算资源投入，而Stockfish现在仍然是顶级引擎是因为在国际象棋领域没有足够的经济激励继续投入计算资源。

• **throw1289312**：指出“苦涩的教训”既涉及学习也涉及搜索，认为Stockfish作为一个搜索优化的例子，同样符合“苦涩的教训”的范畴。

补充讨论：
• “苦涩的教训”在不同技术背景下的适用性和解释有所不同，涉及计算资源、通用方法、手工程序化系统的优劣等多个方面。
• 争议的焦点在于“苦涩的教训”是否适用于所有情境，特别是当计算资源有限或特定领域的技术已经成熟时。
• 讨论中多次提到摩尔定律和计算资源成本问题，显示出对技术进步和经济可行性的关注。

Aug 1, 2025
AI
DESIGN
BITTER LESSON
Does the Bitter Lesson Have Limits?
Recently, “the bitter lesson” is having a moment. Coined in
an essay by Rich Sutton
, the bitter lesson is that, “general methods that leverage computation are ultimately the most effective, and by a large margin.” Why is the lesson bitter? Sutton writes:
The bitter lesson is based on the historical observations that 1) AI researchers have often tried to build knowledge into their agents, 2) this always helps in the short term, and is personally satisfying to the researcher, but 3) in the long run it plateaus and even inhibits further progress, and 4) breakthrough progress eventually arrives by an opposing approach based on scaling computation by search and learning. The eventual success is tinged with bitterness, and often incompletely digested, because it is success over a favored, human-centric approach.
Sutton walks through how the fields of computer chess, computer go, speech recognition, and computer vision have all experienced the bitter lesson.
Lately, people have been citing the bitter lesson a lot.
A Blow to the Human Ego
The first time I read “The Bitter Lesson”, I thought of
Donna Haraway
, one of my professors at UCSC. During a seminar on the history of science, she presented her list of the
four major blows to the human ego
(
which I previously wrote about
):
The Copernican Revolution
, which allowed us to realize we weren’t the center of the universe.
Darwinian thought
, which allowed us to realize we weren’t separate from animals.
Freud’s ideas of the unconscious
, which allowed us to realize that we weren’t in full control of our selves.
Cyborgs
,
robots
, and
automatons
, which allowed us to realize that non-humans could do the work of humans.
These concepts undermined humans’ imagined central position in the universe.
The bitter lesson slots in naturally here; really a sub-point of
cyborgs
, a topic which Haraway has been
exploring for decades
. Within this framework, it’s easy to believe! My instinctual belief reminds me of an exchange from a
2010 RadioLab segment with Neil deGrasse Tyson
:
ROBERT KRULWICH:
Is it your working bias that if I came to you with a new discovery in which we were less important, or a discovery which proposed that we were more important, that you would guess that my scientific discovery that said we are less important is more likely to be right?
NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON:
No doubt about it. That’s correct. Now you call that a bias, but I don’t. I call that track record.
Bitter Skepticism
Surprisingly, the bitter lesson landed on my LinkedIn feed this week. Among the emoji-laden bulleted lists and grindset slop was a new Ethan Mollick piece, “
The Bitter Lesson versus The Garbage Can
”. In it, Mollick contrasts the step-by-step way businesses are building agents with the reality of business processes:
One thing you learn studying (or working in) organizations is that they are all actually a bit of a mess. In fact, one classic organizational theory is actually called the Garbage Can Model. This views organizations as chaotic “garbage cans” where problems, solutions, and decision-makers are dumped in together, and decisions often happen when these elements collide randomly, rather than through a fully rational process. Of course, it is easy to take this view too far - organizations do have structures, decision-makers, and processes that actually matter. It is just that these structures often evolved and were negotiated among people, rather than being carefully designed and well-recorded.
The Garbage Can represents a world where unwritten rules, bespoke knowledge, and complex and undocumented processes are critical. It is this situation that makes AI adoption in organizations difficult, because even though 43% of American workers have used AI at work, they are mostly doing it in informal ways, solving their own work problems. Scaling AI across the enterprise is hard because traditional automation requires clear rules and defined processes; the very things Garbage Can organizations lack.
The bitter lesson is about to be rediscovered, Mollick suggests. “If AI agents can train on outputs alone, any organization that can define quality and provide enough examples might achieve similar results, whether they understand their own processes or not,” he writes. Org charts and workflows are UX for us humans, unneeded by our agents.
But while I found myself quickly accepting the original bitter lesson essay, Mollick’s essay triggered my inner skeptic. Two practical issues immediately arose:
The bitter lesson is dependent on high-quality data.
Data has an embedded perspective. It is not objective. Further, data is
reductive
, a shadow of the information it represents. And many things resist being reduced to data points
1
. Without sufficient data, the bitter lesson cannot be learned.
When Mollick writes, “any organization that can define quality and provide enough examples might achieve similar results,” I immedi

• **itkovian_**：解释了Sutton提出“苦涩的教训”的初衷，指出其核心是比较通用系统和手工程序化系统，而非具体讨论某个系统的优劣。手工程序化系统由于缺乏通用性而难以扩展。

• **Animats**：质疑计算性能提升是否会因为成本问题而达到极限，提到了一些行业中通过商业化运作克服技术困难的例子，如ASML的极紫外光刻技术。

• **jamesblonde**：认为在讨论RAG（检索增强生成）和上下文窗口大小时，不能简单套用“苦涩的教训”。检索的多样性和复杂性使得它不同于纯粹的计算或搜索问题，且当前“苦涩的教训”未必适用于智能体系统。

• **PaulHoule**：提到SAT/SMT求解器的进步，指出其与神经网络一样从1970年代至今都有显著进展，这与“苦涩的教训”强调的计算和通用方法有所不同。

• **thrawa8387336**：质疑“苦涩的教训”的推广背后是否有计算资源销售商的推动，以及那些能够大量购买计算资源的人是否在利用这一观点。

• **pu_pe**：支持“苦涩的教训”，提到Stockfish国际象棋程序的成功部分归功于摩尔定律，并认为Deepmind在国际象棋领域的短暂领先是“苦涩的教训”的一个好例子。

• **strangescript**：指出“苦涩的教训”未明确区分什么是计算“技巧”和什么是真正的架构突破，认为如Transformer这样的创新不可或缺。

• **benreesman**：认为“苦涩的教训”刚提出时具有重要意义，但如今被一些人滥用，变成了一种对LLM和NVIDIA等公司技术的盲目推崇，忽略了其他可能的创新路径。

• **titanomachy**：对“垃圾桶”比喻提出幽默批评，认为其描述组织决策过程并不恰当。

• **quantum_state**：预测可能会有“苦涩的教训2.0”来对当前的“苦涩的教训”进行反思。

• **fdav**：推荐Rodney Brooks的文章“A Better Lesson”，认为有更好的教训值得学习。

• **aydyn**：质疑国际象棋引擎的类比，认为AlphaZero的出现一度超越Stockfish是因为计算资源投入，而Stockfish现在仍然是顶级引擎是因为在国际象棋领域没有足够的经济激励继续投入计算资源。

• **throw1289312**：指出“苦涩的教训”既涉及学习也涉及搜索，认为Stockfish作为一个搜索优化的例子，同样符合“苦涩的教训”的范畴。

补充讨论：
• “苦涩的教训”在不同技术背景下的适用性和解释有所不同，涉及计算资源、通用方法、手工程序化系统的优劣等多个方面。
• 争议的焦点在于“苦涩的教训”是否适用于所有情境，特别是当计算资源有限或特定领域的技术已经成熟时。
• 讨论中多次提到摩尔定律和计算资源成本问题，显示出对技术进步和经济可行性的关注。

data.title: Researchers map where solar energy delivers the biggest climate payoff
data.author: rbanffy
data.article_summary: 一项由罗格斯大学、哈佛大学和石溪大学研究人员合作的研究使用先进计算模型，揭示了太阳能对气候的即时和延迟好处。研究发现，美国太阳能发电量增加15%可每年减少854万吨二氧化碳排放。然而，不同地区的减排效果差异显著，加州、佛罗里达州、中大西洋地区、德州和西南部地区效果显著，而新英格兰和田纳西等地效果有限。研究还显示，太阳能的采用对邻近地区有显著溢出效应，如加州增加太阳能容量还能减少西北和西南地区的二氧化碳排放。该研究为政策制定者和投资者提供了针对性投资太阳能以最大化减排效果的路线图。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于美国太阳能发电增加对二氧化碳减排影响的讨论，以及对太阳能作为气候变化解决方案的评价

不同观点：
• [sabakhoj] 和 [liquidise] 对研究结果表示赞赏，认为太阳能发电增加能显著减少二氧化碳排放，对美国的国家气候目标有积极贡献。他们分享了研究论文和相关图表的链接。
• [smadge] 认为加州有机会成为北美环境和气候行动的典范，例如通过扩大太阳能生产和改善交通网络，但同时指出加州在实现这些目标上存在自我阻碍。
• [pards] 引用研究内容，指出在加州、佛罗里达、中大西洋地区、德州和西南部，小幅增加太阳能发电能显著减少二氧化碳，而在新英格兰、美国中部和田纳西等地影响较小。
• [metonymy] 和 [sophia01] 对研究中缺乏具体地图表示不满，认为文章提到"区域 breakdown"但未提供直观的地图。
• [m0llusk] 提出太阳能技术的预测未能考虑到像德国露台太阳能那样的意外发展，暗示技术和社会趋势有时难以预测。
• [m101] 对研究持批评态度，认为仅关注二氧化碳减排忽略了更广泛的环境问题，并认为太阳能并非解决气候变化的唯一或最佳方案。

补充讨论：
• [rdtsc] 提供了GH项目的数据链接和处理说明，为研究提供了技术支持。
• [searine] 指出该研究由美国纳税人资助，主要来自NIH的11项资助，强调了研究的资金来源。

争议焦点：
• 太阳能发电是否如研究声称的那样对二氧化碳减排有显著效果，尤其是在不同地区的影响差异。
• 研究是否过于狭隘地关注太阳能，而忽略了其他可能更全面的电力生成技术对环境的影响。

Researchers Map Where Solar Energy Delivers the Biggest Climate Payoff
Adobe Stock
Date
July 30, 2025
Media Contact
Patti Zielinski
patti.zielinski@rutgers.edu
Share
Facebook
Twitter
LinkedIn
Reddit
Whatsapp
Email
Print
Using advanced computational modeling, a Rutgers professor, in collaboration with researchers from the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and Stony Brook University, reveal both the immediate and delayed climate benefits of solar power
Increasing solar power generation in the United States by 15% could lead to an annual reduction of 8.54 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions, according to researchers at Rutgers, the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health and Stony Brook University.
The
study
, published in
Science Advances
, found that the climate benefits of solar power differ markedly throughout U.S. regions, pinpointing where clean energy investments return the greatest climate dividends.
In 2023, 60% of
U.S. electricity generation
relied on fossil fuels, while 3.9% came from solar, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Because fossil fuel-generated electricity is a
leading source of carbon dioxide
, or CO2, and harmful air pollutants such as fine particulate matter, expanding solar could not only mitigate CO2 but help
reduce illness, hospitalizations and premature deaths
linked to air pollution exposure.
From a computer science perspective, this study demonstrates the power of harnessing large-scale, high-resolution energy data to generate actionable insights.
Arpita Biswas
Assistant Professor, Department of Computer Science, Rutgers School of Arts and Sciences
Researchers examined five years of hourly electricity generation, demand and emissions data from the Energy Information Administration starting July 1, 2018. They focused on the 13 geographic regions in the United States.
With this
dataset
, the researchers constructed a statistical model to explore how increases in hourly solar energy generation would affect CO2 emissions within a given region and in its neighboring regions.
The study quantified both immediate and delayed emissions reductions resulting from added solar generation. For example, the researchers found that in California, a 15% increase in solar power at noon was associated with a reduction of 147.18 metric tons of CO2 in the region in the first hour and 16.08 metric tons eight hours later.
“It was rewarding to see how advanced computational modeling can uncover not just the immediate, but also the delayed and far-reaching spillover effects of solar energy adoption,” said the lead author
Arpita Biswas
, an assistant professor with the Department of Computer Science at the Rutgers School of Arts and Sciences. “From a computer science perspective, this study demonstrates the power of harnessing large-scale, high-resolution energy data to generate actionable insights. For policymakers and investors, it offers a roadmap for targeting solar investments where emissions reductions are most impactful and where solar energy infrastructure can yield the highest returns.”
The researchers said their methods provide a more nuanced understanding of system-level impacts from solar expansion than previous studies, pinpointing where the benefits of increased solar energy adoption could best be realized. In some areas, such as California, Florida, the mid-Atlantic, the Midwest, Texas and the Southwest, small increases in solar were estimated to deliver large CO2 reductions, while in others, such as New England, the central U.S., and Tennessee, impacts were found to be minimal – even at much larger increases in solar generation.
In addition, the researchers said their study demonstrates the significant spillover effects solar adoption has on neighboring regions, highlighting the value of coordinated clean energy efforts. For example, a 15% increase in solar capacity in California was associated with a reduction of 913 and 1,942 metric tons of CO2 emissions per day in the northwest and southwest regions, respectively.
“
I am very excited about this study because it harnesses the power of data science to offer insights for policymakers and stakeholders in achieving CO2 reduction targets through increased solar generation,” said Francesca Dominici, director of the Harvard Data Science Initiative and Clarence James Gamble Professor of Biostatistics, Population and Data Science and a corresponding author of the study.

data.title: Show HN: TraceRoot – Open-source agentic debugging for distributed services
data.author: xinweihe
data.article_summary: TraceRoot是一个开源调试平台，借助AI分析，通过结合结构化跟踪、日志和源代码上下文，帮助工程师以快10倍的速度解决生产问题。平台具有多代理系统、实时跟踪与日志、结构化日志记录、多资源集成以及对开发者友好的特性。TraceRoot提供了一个类似Cursor的界面，专门用于调试和跟踪，支持与GitHub、Notion等工具集成。用户可以通过TraceRoot Cloud免费试用，或自行部署开源版本。使用前需设置Jaeger容器来存储跟踪和日志，并可通过SDK与应用程序集成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：将Claude代码与MCPs（例如Jaeger、Grafana等工具）集成，并利用其规划功能进行调查的潜在功能和架构设计。

不同观点：
• lmeyerov认为可以将Claude代码与MCPs（如Jaeger、Grafana）以及Git/GH CLIs集成，让Claude的规划器通过这些工具进行调查。他关注的是TraceRoot是否能够在这种设置下做出比现有方案更 clever 的功能，因为他所在的团队正计划实现类似的设置，这是一个实际问题。

• thatrandybrown支持这种用例，但表达了对与OpenAI紧密绑定的担忧，更希望看到一个允许"BYOM"（Bring Your Own Model）的框架，以增加灵活性，避免过度依赖特定AI提供商。

补充讨论：
• lmeyerov的提问表明，他关注的是现有方案（Claude+MCPs）与TraceRoot之间的功能差异，尤其是TraceRoot是否具备现有设置无法实现的独特功能。

• thatrandybrown的评论引出了对技术选型的讨论，强调了开放性和避免单一供应商锁定的问题，提出了BYOM的替代方案以增强系统灵活性。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该在架构设计中紧密绑定特定AI提供商（如OpenAI），还是采用更开放的框架（如BYOM）以支持多种模型。

TraceRoot is an open-source debugging platform that helps engineers fix production issues 10x faster by combining structured traces, logs, and source code context with AI-powered analysis.
Contributing
|
TraceRoot.AI
|
Community
|
SDK
|
Documentation
Join us (
Discord
) in pushing the boundaries of debugging with AI agents.
Please 🌟 Star TraceRoot on GitHub and be instantly notified of new releases.
TraceRoot Framework Design Principles
🤖 Intelligence
The framework enables multi-agent systems to continuously evolve by interacting with environments.
⏰ Real-Time
The framework enables real-time tracing and logging to your applications.
🧠 Structured Information
The framework enables utilizing structured loggings and tracing data to improve the performance of AI agents.
💻 Integration
The framework enables integrating with other sources and tools, such as GitHub, Notion, etc. This provides a seamless experience for you to use the framework in your applications.
😊 Developer Friendly
We also provide a Cursor like interface but specialized for debugging and tracing. You can select the logs and traces you are interested in and ask the framework to help you with the analysis.
Why Use TraceRoot for Your Applications?
We are a community-driven collective comprising over multiple engineers and researchers dedicated to advancing frontier engineering and research in using Multi-Agent Systems to help not only human but also AI agents on debugging, tracing, and root cause analysis.
✅
Multi-Agent System
Multi-Agent system that can be used to solve complex tasks.
✅
Real-Time Tracing and Logging
Enable real-time tracing and logging to your applications.
✅
Structured Logging
Enable structured logging to your applications, which allows better performance of AI agents.
✅
Integration with Multiple Resources
Integrate with other sources and tools, such as GitHub, Notion, etc.
✅
Developer Friendly
We provide a Cursor like interface but specialized for debugging and tracing.

Context Model
Chunking
Explainability

rest/agent
directory
for more details.

TraceRoot Cloud (Recommended)
The fastest and most reliable way to get started with TraceRoot is signing up
for free to
TraceRoot Cloud
for a 7 day trial.
You will have 150k trace + logs storage with 30d retentions, 1.5M LLM tokens,
and AI agent with chat mode.
Self-hosting the open-source deploy (Advanced)
Installation
You can install the latest version of TraceRoot with the following command:
Install the dependencies locally:
git clone https://github.com/traceroot-ai/traceroot.git
cd
traceroot
#
Create and activate a virtual environment
python3.11 -m venv venv
source
venv/bin/activate
#
Install TraceRoot with dependencies excluding optional dependencies
pip install --upgrade pip
pip install -e
.
Local Usage
For local usage, all of your data will be stored locally.
Run the below command to intialize environment variables.
source
.env.development
You can use the TraceRoot framework locally by following the
README.md in the
ui
directory
and
README.md in the
rest
directory
.
Also, you can build the latest docker image and run the docker container by following the
README.md in the
docker
directory
.
This will start the UI at
http://localhost:3000
and the API at
http://localhost:8000
.
Before using the TraceRoot framework, you need to setup the Jaeger docker container at first. It will be used to store the traces and logs and capture the traces and logs from our SDK which is integrated with your applications.

-e COLLECTOR_OTLP_ENABLED=true \
-p 16686:16686 \
-p 14268:14268 \
-p 14250:14250 \
-p 4317:4317 \
-p 4318:4318 \
cr.jaegertracing.io/jaegertracing/jaeger:2.8.0
In local mode, the first step is to go to the integration page and connect with your GitHub account (optional) with your GitHub token.
You also need to put your OpenAI API key in the integration page.

data.title: Dynamic programming bursting balloons
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary:
本文通过一个气球爆破问题解释了动态规划的概念。问题要求在爆破所有气球时最大化获得的金币。由于需要考虑所有可能的爆破顺序，无法使用贪心算法解决。动态规划通过定义状态、基础情况和状态转移来解决问题：

1. **状态**：表示问题的独特配置。
2. **基础情况**：最简单的情况，直接求解。
3. **转移**：定义当前状态与子问题之间的关系。

问题描述是：给定一个数组表示气球，爆破每个气球获得的分数是相邻气球的乘积，求最大化总分。动态规划通过构建表格或使用记忆化递归来高效解决此问题，避免显式构建决策树。动态规划适用于优化问题、包含多个有效解但只有一个最优解、以及需要顺序决策的情况。在此问题中，最优解是按顺序爆破气球以获得最大金币。

Let’s use an example of a dynamic programming problem to illustrate the concept. I didn’t choose an easy example, since it would fit more in the 2D Dynamic Programming category. Introduction What is Dynamic Programming This problem cannot be solved using a greedy approach, as the optimal solution requires considering all possible orders of bursting balloons. We can solve this problem using dynamic programming, for that we need to understand these concepts: State : A state represents a unique configuration of the problem that encapsulates all the necessary information, to make decisions and compute results for that specific sub-problem. Base Case : The base case is the simplest, smallest instance of the problem that can be solved directly without further recursion or iteration, serving as the foundation for building up the solution. Transition : The transition defines the relationship between the current state and smaller sub-problems, specifying how to compute the result for a larger problem using the results of its sub-problems. We can implement this solution either iteratively (building the state bottom-up from the base case to get the next until the optimal one), or recursively (solving problem by applying getting the optimal solution through recursively building top-down the state). We store the state in a table or array in an iterative solution, but in a recursive solution we use memoization , where you store previously computed sub-problems (similar yet different). Problem Statement You are given an array of \(n\) integers representing the coins in balloons 🎈 When you burst a balloon 💥, you gain coins equal to the product of the coins in the balloon and the ones adjacent. If there are no adjacent balloons, we consider virtual balloon with a value of \(1\). For a range of balloons from \(3, 1, 5\): Bursting \(1\) first gives you \(3 \times 1 \times 5 = 15\) coins. Bursting \(3\) first gives you \(1 \times 3 \times 1 = 1\) coins. (using left virtual balloon ) A possibility would be bursting \(1\), then \(5\), then \(3\), which gives you a total of \(3 \times 1 \times 5 + 3 \times 5 \times 1 + 1 \times 3 \times 1 = 33\) coins. But that possibility wouldn’t be the solution as the goal is to maximize the total coins 💰 you can collect by bursting all the balloons. Understanding the problem We can visualize the problem as a tree of choices, where each node represents a state of the balloons and the edges represent the choices made by bursting a balloon. Total Coins: 8 + 1\*3\*1 = 11) class P three K --> R(Total Coins: 13) class R grey L --> S(Total Coins: 9) class S grey M --> T(Total Coins: 35) class T grey N --> U(Total Coins: 33) class U grey O --> V(Total Coins: 13) class V grey P --> W(Total Coins: 11) class W grey We want to be able to identify the optimal path through this tree that maximizes the coins collected. In here for example, we can see that the optimal path is to burst the balloons in the order of 1 , 3 , 5 which gives us a total of 35 coins. But building this tree explicitly would be inefficient, especially for larger arrays of balloons. Instead, we can use dynamic programming to efficiently compute the maximum coins for any subarray of balloons. Dynamic Programming Approach How do we know it’s a dynamic programming problem? The problem of bursting balloons can be classified as a dynamic programming problem due to the following characteristics: Asking for optimization Multiple valid possibilities Only one is optimal (the one that maximizes the coins) Sequential decision-making There is choice to make at each step (which balloon to burst) Future decisions depend on past choices (available balloons change) There’s no greedy

本文通过一个气球爆破问题解释了动态规划的概念。问题要求在爆破所有气球时最大化获得的金币。由于需要考虑所有可能的爆破顺序，无法使用贪心算法解决。动态规划通过定义状态、基础情况和状态转移来解决问题：

1. **状态**：表示问题的独特配置。
2. **基础情况**：最简单的情况，直接求解。
3. **转移**：定义当前状态与子问题之间的关系。

问题描述是：给定一个数组表示气球，爆破每个气球获得的分数是相邻气球的乘积，求最大化总分。动态规划通过构建表格或使用记忆化递归来高效解决此问题，避免显式构建决策树。动态规划适用于优化问题、包含多个有效解但只有一个最优解、以及需要顺序决策的情况。在此问题中，最优解是按顺序爆破气球以获得最大金币。

data.title: When Flatpak's Sandbox Cracks
data.author: dxs
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Flatpak在Linux系统中作为沙箱技术的安全问题。尽管Flatpak通过使用bubblewrap命名空间、系统调用过滤和门户接口来隔离应用程序，理论上提供了一个安全的运行环境，但实际使用中存在漏洞。许多Flatpak应用声明了广泛的权限，如`filesystem=home`或`device=all`，这削弱了沙箱的效果。文章具体介绍了两个安全漏洞：CVE-2024-32462，涉及通过门户接口执行任意主机命令；CVE-2024-42472，涉及利用符号链接获取对敏感文件的访问。此外，Flatpak应用的权限配置复杂，且更新滞后，可能包含过时且有漏洞的库。为增强安全性，文章建议保持Flatpak核心和门户的更新、最小化应用权限、使用工具审核权限、推广安全默认设置并加强教育。未来可以通过自动化沙箱生成工具和持续的运行时扫描来改进安全性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Flatpak的安全性、实用性及其在Linux系统中的角色

不同观点：
• ChocolateGod认为，Flatpak应用常附带filesystem=home权限，可能导致安全隐患，例如通过覆盖sudo配置文件或.desktop文件间接获取root权限。虽然非Flatpak应用也可能有类似问题，但Flatpak给人一种虚假的安全感，可能促使人们下载原本不会考虑的应用。此外，Linux应用开发者缺乏像Android/iOS那样的更新动力，导致安全隐患持续存在。ChocolateGod强调，Flatpak主要是一个应用分发工具，而非安全项目。

• BrenBarn表示，他希望有一个类似Flatpak但不强调安全性的工具。他的主要需求是能够独立于操作系统级别的包管理器更新程序。他对Flatpak的安全性没有特别关注，更看重其在软件更新方面的优势。

• WesolyKubeczek指出，Flatpak的沙盒功能大多是表面功夫，隐私保护有限。他建议一个理想的系统应该允许用户对应用权限进行更细致的控制，例如伪造摄像头、麦克风输入或文件访问路径，而不让应用感知到拒绝或伪造的信息。他认为实现这些功能的组件已经存在，但实际操作较为复杂。

• Fake-name完全反对使用Flatpak、Snap、AppImage等打包项目，认为这些工具只是为了开发者方便，却牺牲了用户体验。他找不到任何理由让用户选择使用这些打包形式的应用。

补充讨论：
• Flatpak的安全性与开发者更新动力之间的矛盾。
• 用户对应用权限控制的细化需求与现有技术实现之间的差距。
• 不同用户对Flatpak的实用性与安全性的认知差异。
• 对Flatpak等打包工具在开发者与用户体验之间的权衡与取舍。

44761760.article_content:
#Linux
#Flatpak
#Security
When Flatpak’s Sandbox Cracks: Real‑Life Security Issues Beyond the Ideal
by
George Whittaker
on July 31, 2025
Introduction
Flatpak promises a secure runtime for Linux applications through container-like isolation, relying on bubblewrap namespaces, syscall filtering, and portal interfaces. In theory, each app should operate inside a strong sandbox, disconnected from the host system. But in reality, experience shows gaps, tiny cracks through which apps may escape with serious consequences.
The Sandbox Promise… and the Reality
Flatpak applications begin life in a highly-restricted environment: no network by default, no access to host files beyond the runtime and a private data directory, limited syscalls, and restricted access to session or system services. Portals provide a controlled channel for granting specific capabilities (e.g. file dialogs, screenshot, printing) without broad privileges.
Yet, many Flatpak packages declare broad permissions like
filesystem=home
,
filesystem=host
, or
device=all
. That effectively grants full read-write access to the user's home directory or even system devices, defeating the purpose of the sandbox in practice. Users often assume that 'sandboxed' means locked-down, but blanket permissions expose them to risk.
Real-World Breakouts from the Sandbox
CVE‑2024‑32462: RequestBackground Portal Abuse
Security researcher Gergo Koteles uncovered a high-severity vulnerability where malicious Flatpak apps could craft a
.desktop
file via the
org.freedesktop.portal.Background.RequestBackground
interface. That tricked Flatpak’s
--command=
parsing into injecting
bwrap
arguments (e.g.
--bind
). This allowed arbitrary host commands to execute outside the sandbox boundary. Versions before 1.10.9, 1.12.9, 1.14.6, and 1.15.8 were affected. Patched in the listed versions and mitigated in xdg-desktop-portal 1.18.4 and newer.
CVE‑2024‑42472: Persistent Data Symlink Exploit
A Flatpak flag,
--persist
(or
persistent=
in manifest), allows apps writable storage within their data directory. But if a malicious install replaces that directory with a symlink pointing to sensitive host folders (e.g.
~/.ssh
), the sandbox mount entry follows it into the real filesystem, giving the app unintended access to files outside its name-spaced area. All versions up to 1.14.8 and 1.15.x ≤ 1.15.9 are vulnerable; patched in 1.14.10 and 1.15.10+.
Policy Complexity and Ecosystem Slip-Ups
A detailed study of hundreds of Flatpak and Snap packages found that nearly 42% of Flatpak apps either override the supposed isolation or misconfigure sandboxing, resulting in overprivilege or potential escape paths. Crafting fine-grained sandbox policy is hard, and mistakes slip through easily.
Additionally, Flathub apps often bundle runtimes with outdated libraries, even when fixed upstream months earlier. Users of those apps remain exposed because the sandboxed apps include vulnerable binaries frozen in time.
What Administrators and Developers Should Do
Keep Flatpak Core and Portals Up to Date
Always install a supported Flatpak version, at minimum 1.14.6 (or 1.10.9 / 1.12.9 depending on patch branch) or later, to close CVE‑2024‑32462. Make sure xdg-desktop-portal is at 1.18.4 or newer. Similarly, upgrade past 1.15.10 to guard against the persistent symlink issue.
Minimize Granted Permissions
Avoid blanket access declarations, especially
filesystem=host
or
device=all
. Only allow app isolation to loosen enough to perform necessary functionality. Use portals instead of file permissions wherever possible.
Audit with Tools
Use utilities like Flatseal to inspect and adjust active permissions on installed apps. Encourage app packagers to use narrower sandbox manifests and thorough static/dynamic analysis tools before publishing.
Promote Secure Defaults and Education
Ecosystem maintainers (such as Flathub) should ship more restrictive default permissions. App developers should be educated about sandbox risk and least-privilege policy design.
Systemic Imbalances and Technical Gaps
Ease vs. Security
: Usable app behavior sometimes requires broad permissions. Stricter defaults can break functionality, leading developers to relax policies.
Explorer Exploits
: Portals themselves become targets, as seen in CVE‑2024‑32462, any interface bridging sandbox and host is a potential avenue. Portal hardening needs investment.
Update Lag
: Flatpak runtimes often lag behind distro updates, so vulnerabilities in built-in libraries remain unpatched for months, exposing users unknowingly.
Lack of Automation
: Developers lack tools that suggest minimal permission sets tied to actual app behavior patterns.
Where Things Could Improve
Automated Sandbox Generators
: Tools that analyze an app’s behavior during testing and suggest minimal manifest permissions.
Enhanced Portal Checks
: Improved validation on portal input parameters to reject dangerous command patterns.
Continuous Runtime Scanning
: Flathub or distributions could periodicall

data.title: A DH106 1A Comet has been restored at the de Havilland Aircraft Museum
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了世界上第一架商用喷气式飞机——德哈维兰DH106彗星号（Comet G-ALYP）的首航历史及其影响。1952年5月2日，这架飞机从伦敦机场起飞，历时23小时，中途停留五次，飞行7000英里抵达约翰内斯堡。这标志着航空旅行进入喷气时代，提供了比螺旋桨飞机更舒适和快速的体验。然而，由于一系列事故，彗星号机队很快被停飞并进行破坏性测试。如今，德哈维兰飞机博物馆恢复了该飞机的内饰，让人们可以一窥当年的飞行体验。博物馆还展示了二战时期的蚊式战斗机原型等珍贵航空文物。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：De Havilland Comet飞机的历史、技术特点、保存现状及设计缺陷

不同观点：
• [zabzonk] 分享了20世纪60年代乘坐Comet 4从雅典飞往尼科西亚的个人经历，感觉像是在乘坐老式的火车车厢，可能与运营公司Olympic Airways的维护有关。
• [betamaxthetape] 指出在英国国家收藏中心保存的另一架Comet 4B变种飞机目前不向公众开放，引用了相关来源加以证明。
• [buildsjets] 提到自1995年以来在西雅图的飞行博物馆中有一架DH106 Mk4C正在修复，但由于疫情等原因，修复工作自2019年以来几乎停滞，且博物馆可能在几年后失去租赁权。
• [rwmj] 介绍了其当地一家飞机博物馆中的Comet展品，包括已经修复的方形窗Comet和可供参观的Comet驾驶舱，并提到博物馆还有其他经典飞机如Mosquito和Chipmunk。

补充讨论：
• [SoftTalker] 提到关于Comet原始设计的方形窗口导致结构裂缝的传言，并指出尽管有争议，现代大多数增压飞机还是采用了圆形或椭圆形的窗口设计以减少应力集中。
• [dangle1] 认为Comet的结构问题本可以更好地预防，同时指出其发动机嵌入机翼的设计可能导致火灾和引擎故障等问题，甚至比引擎安装在挂架上的飞机有更高的风险。

De Havilland Aircraft Museum, England

Today, jet-powered plane travel is easy to take for granted. We’re used to that surge of speed along the runway that pins us to our seats, those moments when we burst through ominous clouds into bright blue skies, and the gentle pings warning us to fasten seatbelts. And we’re used to arriving at our destination in one piece.
But commercial jet travel is only 73 years old. Britain’s late Queen Elizabeth II was already the monarch when the de Havilland DH106 1A Comet G-ALYP took off from London Airport — as Heathrow was then known — about 3 p.m. on May 2, 1952, carrying the world’s first fare-paying jet passengers. Over the next 23 hours, with five stops along the route, it made its way 7,000 miles south to Johannesburg.
That flight marked a huge breakthrough in comfort and speed, compared to even the era’s top-of-the-range propeller aircraft like the Lockheed Constellation. Gone were the constant vibrations and the sonic assault from piston engines. The world had suddenly, irreversibly, entered the jet age.
And the first jet-plane builder to claim a place in the skies, beating out United States rivals like Boeing, was the British aviation company de Havilland. That advantage wouldn’t last: the original Comet DH106 enjoyed only a brief reign before a series of catastrophes led its entire fleet to be pulled out of service and then tested to destruction or left to rot.
The DH106 1A Comet has been restored at the de Havilland Aircraft Museum near London.
Barry Neild/CNN
Generations later, the only way to experience what it was like on board those first Comets is to look at grainy black-and-white film footage or color publicity photos of smiling families sitting on board DH106 1As.
Or at least, until recently, those images were all we had. Now a gang of enthusiasts has painstakingly pieced one of those pioneering jetliners back together — with thrilling results.

The DH106 represented a revolution in air transport, being smoother and less noisy than the propeller planes that came before. Even in standard class, seating was roomy with plenty of leg space.

The controls look complicated but would've been familiar to the pilots of the day, many of whom had military aviation backgrounds, having flown during World War II.

The cockpit also included a table for the navigator, who would manually calculate position based on speed and direction. An astrolabe was fitted in the ceiling of the plane so that the navigator could also take position readings using the stars.

Jet power:
The Comet DH106 1A was powered by four de Havilland Ghost turbo jets which were embedded into the wings.

The de Havilland Aircraft Museum is also home to the only prototype World War II plane still in existence. The Mosquito fighter, which was made on the site of the museum, was constructed from wood.

After fatal incidents involving the Comet, engineers rigorously tested the aircraft's fuselage and found that its rivet holes couldn't handle regular changes in pressure, leading to catastrophic breaches.

Located in a belt of farmland and greenery northwest of London, close to the eternally congested M25 highway that encircles the British capital, it’s easy to miss. There are signposts, but they point to a narrow lane between hedgerows that looks as if it leads to a farmyard or dead end.

data.article_summary: Atlassian近日通过预录视频解雇了150名员工，主要来自其欧洲运营部门，视频后员工需等待15分钟以确认是否被裁。被裁员工的电脑立即被封锁，但将获得六个月的工资补偿。此次裁员是由于公司向AI客服解决方案转型，客户对复杂支持的需求减少。Atlassian联合创始人Mike Cannon-Brookes发送了该视频，而另一创始人Scott Farquhar此前曾表示AI将深刻改变澳大利亚，并倡导广泛应用AI。此举引发员工对公司沟通方式冷淡的批评。此前，澳大利亚联邦银行也因AI推广而裁减了至少45个岗位。

Atlassian terminates 150 staff with pre-recorded video, AI customer contact solutions rolled out
Major Australian tech company Atlassian has terminated 150 staff with a pre-recorded video, as the company pushes its AI-embedded customer contact solutions.
Daniel Croft
•
Wed, 30 Jul 2025
•
Digital Transformation

Atlassian CEO and co-founder Mike Cannon-Brookes sent the video titled “Restructuring the CSS Team: A Difficult Decision for Our Future” to staff on Wednesday morning (30 July), informing them that 150 staff had been made redundant. The video reportedly did not make it seem that the decision was difficult, but rather said it would allow its staff “to say goodbye”.
The video itself did not announce who was leaving, but it told employees they would have to wait 15 minutes for an email about their employment. Those who were terminated had their laptops blocked immediately. They reportedly will receive six months’ pay.

saying that Cannon-Brooke’s overshared that it would be difficult to axe its European staff due to contract arrangements, but that the company had already begun moving in that direction.

.

data.title: Tested: Microsoft Recall can still capture credit cards and passwords
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: Microsoft Recall是一款通过AI截屏帮助用户搜索电脑操作的应用，尽管声称能过滤敏感信息如信用卡号和密码，但测试显示其过滤功能并不完善。例如，它未能过滤掉某些无明显标识的信用卡信息和密码文件，甚至在某些情况下截取了PayPal用户名。虽然过滤功能在一些场景下有效，如银行账户信息屏蔽，但整体上仍存在漏洞，可能导致个人信息泄露，成为不法分子的目标。微软的默认设置鼓励用户启用Recall，但其安全性仍不足，存在隐私风险。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Recall是否应被视为间谍软件，以及其功能是否必要和有效。

不同观点：
• Bender认为Recall应被视为间谍软件，因为它会记录设备上的所有数据。Bender以幽默的方式建议将所有数据转换为恶搞内容（如RickRolls）以引起关注，暗示这种工具对隐私的侵犯。

• VohuMana对Recall的工作原理不太了解，但对隐藏Google密码管理器而不隐藏文本文件中的密码表示质疑。VohuMana认为程序可能需要明确指示应从Recall中隐藏，并对Recall的功能持怀疑态度，认为其像是“寻找问题的解决方案”，即不认为有大量数据需要被截屏。

补充讨论：
• VohuMana提出了一种替代方案，认为帮助用户找到历史访问网站可以通过解析和总结网页内容来实现，而不必进行屏幕截图。这表明了对Recall当前实现方式的质疑以及对隐私保护的关注。

• 争议的焦点在于Recall的功能设计是否合理，以及其对用户隐私的影响。Bender更关注隐私侵犯问题，而VohuMana则对功能的实用性和必要性提出质疑。

Our tests have shown there are ways to get around the promised security improvements
Avram Piltch
Fri 1 Aug 2025
//
